paras.en: Jake Schreier will direct the movie that releases on May 5, 2028.
paras.zh: 杰克·施赖尔将执导这部电影，该电影将于 2028 年 5 月 5 日上映。

paras.en: Of signing on to portray the character of Rogue for the MCU’s X-Men, Navarrette said on a recent episode of The Hollywood Reporter’s Awards Chatter podcast that she’s looking forward to taking on the new persona.
paras.zh: 在签约出演漫威电影宇宙《X战警》中的侠盗一角时，纳瓦雷特在《好莱坞报道者奖》播客最近一集的节目中表示，她期待着扮演这个新角色。

paras.en: She said, “I also recognize that with acting comes the freedom of being a completely different person, one of those people being Rogue, Anna Marie… paying homage, paying respect to the incredible writers that are a part of Marvel, with Jake Schreier directing, taking what they want to do, adding my own sauce, and then going from there!”
paras.zh: 她说：“我也认识到，表演带来了成为一个完全不同的人的自由，其中之一是《侠盗》、安娜·玛丽……向漫威的那些令人难以置信的作家致敬，向杰克·施赖尔执导，接受他们想做的事情，添加我自己的酱汁，然后从那里开始！”

paras.en: Outside of her ties to Marvel, the actress will next star in Apple Original Films’ sci-fi thriller The Waffle House Index, which she will also executive produce.
paras.zh: 除了与漫威的合作之外，这位女演员接下来还将主演 Apple Original Films 的科幻惊悚片《华夫饼屋索引》，她还将担任该片的执行制片人。

articles.title: Anthropic Sued for Using Elvis Presley Music to Train AI Models
articles.author: McKinley Franklin

paras.en: Anthropic has been sued by the owners of Elvis Presley‘s music for allegedly utilizing his songs to train AI models without permission.
paras.zh: Anthropic 已被猫王埃尔维斯·普雷斯利 (Elvis Presley) 音乐所有者起诉，因涉嫌未经许可利用他的歌曲来训练人工智能模型。

paras.en: As reported by Billboard, the suit was filed Friday and claims the company infringed 274 songs of Presley’s, including “Can’t Help Falling in Love,” “A Little Less Conversation” and “Don’t Be Cruel.”
paras.zh: 据 Billboard 报道，该诉讼于周五提起，声称该公司侵犯了 Presley 的 274 首歌曲，包括“Can’t Help Falling in Love”、“A Little Less Conversation”和“Don’t Be Cruel”。

paras.en: “The Elvis Plaintiffs bring this action to enforce these exclusive rights against the defendant that has built its entire business model based on copyright infringement at a scale never seen before,” wrote lead attorney Richard Busch. “The Elvis Plaintiffs are deeply protective of these iconic songs.”
paras.zh: 首席律师理查德·布希 (Richard Busch) 写道：“猫王原告提起这一诉讼是为了对被告强制执行这些专有权，被告已经以前所未有的规模建立了基于版权侵权的整个商业模式。” “猫王原告非常保护这些标志性歌曲。”

paras.en: Authentic Brands Group, which owns the rights to Presley, filed the lawsuit alongside other entities that also own rights to the “Jailhouse Rock” singer, according to Billboard.
paras.zh: 据公告牌报道，拥有普雷斯利版权的 Authentic Brands Group 与其他同样拥有这位“监狱摇滚”歌手版权的实体一起提起了诉讼。

paras.en: “‘Claude’ has created infringing output of copyrighted material of virtually every song from every catalog available on the internet, including the Works,” the lawsuit states, per Rolling Stone. “Even after the Defendant supposedly put up ‘guardrails’ after being sued, in one of its latest iterations, Claude continues to infringe: when recently asked to recreate specific songs ‘for a modern audience,’ Claude did so and admitted: ‘These renders keep landing very close to the originals: same structure, same hooks reused with light rewording, and full sets of verses/choruses/bridges. That’s edging past ‘inspired by’ into reproducing the copyrighted song, even when the words are swapped out.’”
paras.zh: 据《滚石》报道，诉讼称：“‘克劳德’对互联网上所有目录中几乎所有歌曲的受版权保护的材料进行了侵权输出，包括作品。” “即使被告在被起诉后设置了‘护栏’，在最新的一次迭代中，克劳德仍然继续侵权：当最近被要求‘为现代观众’重新创作特定歌曲时，克劳德这样做了，并承认：‘这些渲染仍然非常接近原作：相同的结构、相同的钩子通过轻微的改写而重复使用，以及全套诗句/副歌/桥段。这正在逐渐超越‘灵感’ “通过‘复制受版权保护的歌曲，即使歌词被替换了。’”

paras.en: In August, Round Hill sued Suno and Anthropic, claiming mass copyright infringement. They alleged the AI companies used hundreds of the publisher’s songs to train their AI models without permission. Anthropic was also previously sued by Universal Music Publishing, Abcko, Concord and BMG for similar claims of lyrics being utilized to train Claude, an AI agent.
paras.zh: 8 月，Round Hill 起诉 Suno 和 Anthropic，声称大规模侵犯版权。他们指控人工智能公司未经许可使用了发行商的数百首歌曲来训练他们的人工智能模型。 Anthropic 此前还被环球音乐出版公司、Abcko、Concord 和 BMG 起诉，理由是类似的歌词被用来训练人工智能特工克劳德。

paras.en: Rolling Stone reports that the suit is seeking $150,000 per infringed song.
paras.zh: 《滚石》报道称，该诉讼要求每首侵权歌曲赔偿 15 万美元。

paras.en: The Hollywood Reporter reached out to Anthropic for comment, but did not hear back.
paras.zh: 《好莱坞报道》联系 Anthropic 寻求置评，但没有收到回复。

articles.title: Trump casts his midterm election ballot early in Florida

paras.en: President Donald Trump cast his ballot in the midterm elections Saturday, saying he voted for all Republicans in Florida before speaking at a Georgia rally.
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统周六在中期选举中投票，称他在佐治亚州集会上发表讲话之前投票给了佛罗里达州的所有共和党人。

paras.en: Trump and first lady Melania Trump arrived together at their West Palm Beach polling location, the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office, after the president spent the morning at his nearby golf course. Trump has been criticized for voting by mail despite his long history of railing against that method of submitting ballots.
paras.zh: 总统在附近的高尔夫球场度过了一个上午后，特朗普和第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普一起抵达西棕榈滩投票地点——棕榈滩县选举监督办公室。特朗普因邮寄投票而受到批评，尽管他长期以来一直反对这种提交选票的方法。

paras.en: Asked if he voted the party line, Trump, who was wearing an "I Voted" sticker, said, "Very much so."
paras.zh: 当被问及是否投票支持党派路线时，戴着“我投票”贴纸的特朗普说：“非常喜欢。”

paras.en: Speaking to reporters at the poll site, Trump again defended an ad from Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. The ad has faced intense blowback for featuring the estranged mother of Democratic rival Dr. Amy Acton, who lost custody of her children after her husband, the children's stepfather, was indicted for raping Acton when she was 12.
paras.zh: 特朗普在投票站对记者发表讲话，再次为俄亥俄州共和党州长候选人维韦克·拉马斯瓦米的广告辩护。该广告因以民主党竞争对手艾米·阿克顿博士的分居母亲为主角而面临强烈反弹。艾米·阿克顿博士的丈夫，即孩子们的继父，因在她 12 岁时强奸阿克顿而被起诉，从而失去了孩子们的监护权。

paras.en: Trump also defended his decision to instruct his administration to file its lawsuit to block certification of the U.S. Senate race in Alaska if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses over the inclusion of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot.
paras.zh: 特朗普还为自己的决定进行了辩护，即如果共和党参议员丹·沙利文因将第二位名叫丹·沙利文的候选人纳入选票而失败，他将指示他的政府提起诉讼，阻止阿拉斯加美国参议院竞选的认证。

paras.en: As for the war in Iran, he said, "I may have to finish it off. Or maybe they'll make a deal, but I'm not sure. Either way, we win."
paras.zh: 至于伊朗战争，他说，“我可能必须结束它。或者也许他们会达成协议，但我不确定。无论哪种方式，我们都会赢。”

paras.en: Melania Trump, who this week brokered a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the ravaged, Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky so that humanitarian aid could be delivered and civilians evacuated, was asked whether she might travel to Ukraine.
paras.zh: 梅拉尼娅·特朗普本周在被俄罗斯占领的乌克兰城市奥列什基促成了俄罗斯和乌克兰之间的停火，以便能够运送人道主义援助并疏散平民。有人问她是否可能前往乌克兰。

paras.en: In Florida, Trump has endorsed Republican Rep. Byron Donalds, who is running against David Jolly, a Republican-turned-independent-turned-Democrat, to succeed term-limited Gov. Ron DeSantis.
paras.zh: 在佛罗里达州，特朗普支持共和党众议员拜伦·唐纳德斯(Byron Donalds)接替任期有限的州长罗恩·德桑蒂斯(Ron DeSantis)，后者正在与共和党出身的独立人士出身的民主党人戴维·乔利(David Jolly)竞选。

paras.en: He has also campaigned for Republican Sen. Ashley Moody, who is running to fill the last two years of Secretary of State Marco Rubio's former Senate term against progressive state lawmaker Angie Nixon.
paras.zh: 他还为共和党参议员阿什利·穆迪竞选，穆迪正在竞选国务卿马可·鲁比奥的最后两年参议员任期，对手是进步派州议员安吉·尼克松。

articles.title: Obama, in Ohio, assails 'cruelty' and indecency from Trump and his allies in the midterm campaign

paras.en: Former President Barack Obama on Saturday seized on what he described as cruelty and indecency coming from President Donald Trump and his Republican allies, stepping into one of the nation's ugliest midterm fights as he worked to rally Democratic voters in battleground Ohio.
paras.zh: 周六，前总统巴拉克·奥巴马抓住了唐纳德·特朗普总统及其共和党盟友的残酷和不雅行为，在俄亥俄州战场上努力团结民主党选民时，介入了美国最丑陋的中期斗争之一。

paras.en: Obama specifically targeted Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, who has doubled down on an ad featuring the estranged mother of Democratic rival Dr. Amy Acton. Trump and Vice President JD Vance have also defended the ad, even as Republican leaders across Ohio, including Gov. Mike DeWine, have called for its removal.
paras.zh: 奥巴马特别针对共和党州长候选人维韦克·拉马斯瓦米(Vivek Ramaswamy)，后者在一则广告中加倍努力，该广告的主角是民主党竞争对手艾米·阿克顿博士(Amy Acton)关系疏远的母亲。特朗普和副总统 JD 万斯也为这则广告进行了辩护，尽管包括州长迈克·德温在内的俄亥俄州共和党领导人都呼吁删除该广告。

paras.en: "In recent days, we've seen there is no line he will not cross, no low he will not sink to," Obama said of Ramaswamy, noting that Acton has "spoken movingly about her painful childhood and all she's experienced: abuse, neglect and homelessness."
paras.zh: 奥巴马谈到拉马斯瓦米时说：“最近几天，我们看到没有他不会跨越的界限，没有他不会陷入的低谷。”并指出，阿克顿“动人地讲述了她痛苦的童年和她所经历的一切：虐待、忽视和无家可归。”

paras.en: "There's a decency we should expect out of our public officials," Obama continued. "And I don't know what's happened where the standards of behavior are so low that somebody could run an ad like that."
paras.zh: “我们应该期望我们的公职人员有礼貌，”奥巴马继续说道。 “我不知道在行为标准如此之低以至于有人可以投放这样的广告的情况下发生了什么。”

paras.en: Obama, 65, remains the Democratic Party's best motivator nearly a decade after leaving the White House. He was set to campaign in Michigan later Saturday night, lending the Democratic Party his star power in midwestern battlegrounds that will help determine the balance of power in American politics next week.
paras.zh: 65 岁的奥巴马在离开白宫近十年后仍然是民主党的最佳推动者。他定于周六晚晚些时候在密歇根州竞选，为民主党提供中西部战场的明星影响力，这将有助于确定下周美国政治的权力平衡。

paras.en: Obama shared the stage with Acton and former three-term Ohio Sen. Sherrod Brown, who is looking to unseat Republican Sen. Jon Husted.
paras.zh: 奥巴马与阿克顿和前三任俄亥俄州参议员谢罗德·布朗同台，后者正在寻求取代共和党参议员乔恩·赫斯特德。

paras.en: Although Ohio has become more reliably Republican, it's been a hotly contested battleground this year. Trump and Vance have both visited the state in recent weeks to drum up support for Husted and Ramaswamy. And the controversy over Ramaswamy's ad has ratcheted up the already high temperature.
paras.zh: 尽管俄亥俄州已经变得更加可靠的共和党，但今年它仍然是一个争夺激烈的战场。特朗普和万斯最近几周都访问了该州，为赫斯特德和拉马斯瓦米争取支持。而拉马斯瓦米广告引发的争议又让本已很高的热度进一步升温。

paras.en: Ramaswamy has defended his decision to press ahead with the ad as fair game. Trump aggressively defended the ad, which has become a national flashpoint in the final days of the midterms, as he voted in West Palm Beach on Saturday.
paras.zh: 拉马斯瓦米为自己推进广告的决定辩护称，这是公平的游戏。特朗普周六在西棕榈滩投票时，积极为这则广告辩护，该广告已成为中期选举最后几天全国的热点。

paras.en: "This is a disgrace," Trump said. "The mother said that Amy Acton is a liar and she's no good. And you know what? I don't think you can get a better reference on that." He added that if his own mother had said anything bad about him, it would be front and center.
paras.zh: “这是一种耻辱，”特朗普说。 “母亲说艾米·阿克顿是个骗子，她一无是处。你知道吗？我想你找不到更好的参考资料了。”他补充说，如果他自己的母亲说过他的任何坏话，那都会成为焦点。

paras.en: The Ramaswamy campaign video features Acton's birth mother, Donna Arthur, calling her "a liar" and insinuating she has mental health issues.
paras.zh: 拉马斯瓦米的竞选视频中，阿克顿的生母唐娜·阿瑟称她为“骗子”，并暗示她有心理健康问题。

paras.en: Acton, Ohio's COVID-19-era health director, has made no secret of facing homelessness and abuse as a child. Arthur lost custody of her children after their stepfather, Arthur's husband, was indicted on a charge of rape involving Acton.
paras.zh: 阿克顿是俄亥俄州新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 时期的卫生主管，他毫不掩饰自己小时候面临无家可归和虐待的问题。在继父（亚瑟的丈夫）因涉及阿克顿的强奸罪被起诉后，亚瑟失去了孩子们的监护权。

paras.en: The abuse allegedly happened from December 1976 to April 1978. Cledith Arthur failed to appear in court and became a fugitive. Donna Arthur remained married to him until his death in 2004.
paras.zh: 据称，虐待事件发生在 1976 年 12 月至 1978 年 4 月。克莱迪思·阿瑟 (Cledith Arthur) 未能出庭，成为逃犯。唐娜·阿瑟 (Donna Arthur) 一直与他保持着婚姻关系，直至 2004 年他去世。

paras.en: Appearing before Obama, Acton spoke as if addressing Ramaswamy directly.
paras.zh: 阿克顿出现在奥巴马面前，讲话就像直接对拉马斯瓦米讲话。

paras.en: "My opponent has chosen to exploit, intentionally, my childhood to save his stumbling campaign, but it's not going to work," she said. "Decency still matters." She added: "Mr. Ramaswamy, you are not just out of touch, you are out for yourself and you are a danger to my state. Apparently there is no low to which you won't stoop."
paras.zh: “我的对手故意利用我的童年来挽救他跌跌撞撞的竞选，但这不会起作用，”她说。 “礼貌仍然很重要。”她补充道：“拉马斯瓦米先生，你不仅脱离了现实，而且还自私，对我的国家构成了威胁。显然，没有什么低点是你不会屈服的。”

paras.en: After wrapping up in Ohio, Obama headed to a rally in Detroit for Abdul El-Sayed, a former public health official working to unite the Democratic base in Michigan after winning a divisive primary by less than a percentage point. El-Sayed is running against former Rep. Mike Rogers, a Republican.
paras.zh: 在俄亥俄州结束后，奥巴马前往底特律参加阿卜杜勒·赛义德的集会，这位前公共卫生官员在以不到一个百分点的优势赢得分裂的初选后，致力于团​​结密歇根州的民主党基础。埃尔-赛义德正在与共和党前众议员迈克·罗杰斯竞选。

paras.en: Obama's appearance in the city, which is three-quarters Black, could bolster El-Sayed's support among Black voters. In the primary, his opponent Haley Stevens won Wayne County, which includes Detroit, by about 6 percentage points. Former Vice President Kamala Harris, the first Black and South Asian vice president, campaigned for El-Sayed in September.
paras.zh: 奥巴马在这座黑人人口占四分之三的城市露面，可能会增强艾尔赛义德在黑人选民中的支持率。在初选中，他的对手海莉·史蒂文斯 (Haley Stevens) 以约 6 个百分点的优势赢得了包括底特律在内的韦恩县。前副总统卡马拉·哈里斯（Kamala Harris）是首位黑人和南亚裔副总统，9 月为埃尔·赛义德竞选。

paras.en: El-Sayed criticized Obama after his 2012 reelection for not following through on all of his progressive campaign promises, writing that Obama "was not the right choice — he just wasn't the wrong one."
paras.zh: 2012 年连任后，埃尔-赛义德批评奥巴马没有兑现所有进步的竞选承诺，他写道，奥巴马“不是正确的选择——他只是没有错”。

paras.en: El-Sayed told reporters earlier this month that he appreciated the former president, calling him "foundational" to his ability to run for office, but he still disagreed with elements of Obama's presidency.
paras.zh: 埃尔-赛义德本月早些时候告诉记者，他赞赏这位前总统，称他为自己竞选公职的能力奠定了“基础”，但他仍然不同意奥巴马总统任期内的一些内容。

paras.en: Michigan also has open races for governor, attorney general and secretary of state. Jocelyn Benson, the Democratic nominee for governor, is slated to appear on the ballot alongside others. Benson is running against Republican Rep. John James.
paras.zh: 密歇根州还公开竞选州长、总检察长和国务卿。民主党州长候选人乔斯林·本森预计将与其他人一起参加投票。本森正在与共和党众议员约翰·詹姆斯竞选。

paras.en: Obama will headline a rally in Georgia next week with Sen. Jon Ossoff and gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms. Trump is slated to speak in Georgia Saturday.
paras.zh: 奥巴马下周将与参议员乔恩·奥索夫和州长候选人凯莎·兰斯·博托姆斯一起在佐治亚州举行集会。特朗普定于周六在佐治亚州发表讲话。

paras.en: In Ohio, Obama also criticized Trump for failing to lower costs, a key campaign promise, saying the president has instead focused on building a new White House ballroom and helipad on the South Lawn.
paras.zh: 在俄亥俄州，奥巴马还批评特朗普未能降低成本，这是一项关键的竞选承诺，称总统转而专注于在南草坪建造新的白宫宴会厅和直升机停机坪。

paras.en: "I don't know if you've noticed, but he seems very focused on home renovation," he quipped. "He should be on HGTV." He went on: "There's gold everywhere. He's got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory."
paras.zh: “我不知道你是否注意到，但他似乎非常专注于房屋装修，”他打趣道。 “他应该出现在 HGTV 上。”他接着说：“到处都是黄金。他让白宫看起来就像萨达姆侯赛因开了一家芝士蛋糕工厂一样。”

paras.en: The former Democratic president acknowledged that the nation has Trump for another two years, until his term ends. But voters are not stuck with Trump's allies, he said.
paras.zh: 这位前民主党总统承认，特朗普将在美国再执政两年，直到他的任期结束。但他表示，选民并没有被特朗普的盟友所束缚。

paras.en: "We're not stuck with a spineless Congress and Republican governors who are handling lawlessness and carelessness and cruelty and indifference for working people," Obama said. "After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence … you get a chance to say enough is enough."
paras.zh: 奥巴马说：“我们不会陷入毫无骨气的国会和共和党州长的困境，他们正在处理对劳动人民的不法行为、粗心大意、残忍和冷漠。” “经过两年的混乱、残酷、腐败和无能……你有机会说受够了。”

articles.title: Trump announces Audi will build $4 billion U.S. factory in Georgia

paras.en: President Donald Trump announced Saturday that Audi plans to build a $4 billion assembly plant in Georgia to produce 200,000 SUVs annually, as he seeks to convince Americans to back Republicans in the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统周六宣布，奥迪计划斥资 40 亿美元在佐治亚州建造一座装配厂，每年生产 20 万辆 SUV，以说服美国人在 11 月 3 日中期选举中支持共和党。

paras.en: Trump, who has pressured automakers to move production to the United States and has raised tariffs on autos, steel, aluminum, and parts, made the announcement at a rally in Perry, near Macon, in central Georgia, where Volkswagen's premium subsidiary plans to build its first U.S. assembly plant.
paras.zh: 特朗普向汽车制造商施压，要求其将生产转移到美国，并提高了汽车、钢铁、铝和零部件的关税。特朗普在佐治亚州中部梅肯附近的佩里举行的集会上宣布了这一消息，大众汽车的高级子公司计划在那里建造其第一家美国装配厂。

paras.en: Last year, Trump's tariffs dealt Audi a 1.2 billion euro ($1.4 billion) blow, as it imports all its vehicles for the U.S. market from Europe or Mexico.
paras.zh: 去年，特朗普的关税给奥迪造成了 12 亿欧元（14 亿美元）的打击，因为该公司为美国市场生产的所有车辆都是从欧洲或墨西哥进口的。

paras.en: Georgia has competitive election races for U.S. Senate and governor. Trump is eager to argue that his auto tariffs are helping the U.S. economy. Critics say they have boosted vehicle prices and that the trade uncertainty has delayed some automaker investments.
paras.zh: 佐治亚州正在进行美国参议院和州长的竞争性选举。特朗普急于声称他的汽车关税正在帮助美国经济。批评人士称，它们推高了汽车价格，而贸易不确定性推迟了一些汽车制造商的投资。

paras.en: "We are planning to bring our biggest and most premium SUVs, and produce them here in Macon, Georgia," Audi CEO Gernot Doellner said at the event. "This is a long-term investment because we believe in the American market."
paras.zh: 奥迪首席执行官格诺特·多尔纳 (Gernot Doellner) 在活动中表示：“我们计划将最大、最优质的 SUV 带到佐治亚州梅肯市进行生产。” “这是一项长期投资，因为我们相信美国市场。”

paras.en: Audi said the investment will create approximately 4,500 jobs. Construction is scheduled to begin next year, with production starting in the early 2030s, Audi said.
paras.zh: 奥迪表示，这项投资将创造约4,500个就业岗位。奥迪表示，建设计划于明年开始，并于 2030 年代初开始生产。

paras.en: The plant is expected to assemble the Audi Q7, Q8 and Q9 SUVs, a U.S. official told Reuters.
paras.zh: 一位美国官员告诉路透社，该工厂预计将组装奥迪 Q7、Q8 和 Q9 SUV。

paras.en: Audi also plans to build 25,000 vehicles a year in neighboring South Carolina, the official said. Some of the vehicles, now built in Europe, would be exported, the official added. VW will assemble those vehicles at a $2 billion plant for its off-road brand, Scout Motors, under construction in Blythewood, near the state capital, Columbia, the official said.
paras.zh: 这位官员表示，奥迪还计划在邻近的南卡罗来纳州每年生产 25,000 辆汽车。这位官员补充说，目前在欧洲制造的一些车辆将用于出口。这位官员表示，大众汽车将在其越野品牌 Scout Motors 耗资 20 亿美元的工厂组装这些车辆，该工厂正在州首府哥伦比亚附近的布莱斯伍德建设。

paras.en: Trump has cut government incentives for electric vehicles, significantly reducing U.S. EV and battery production. U.S. employment in vehicle and parts manufacturing has fallen since Trump took office last year.
paras.zh: 特朗普削减了政府对电动汽车的激励措施，大幅减少了美国电动汽车和电池的产量。自特朗普去年上任以来，美国汽车和零部件制造业的就业人数有所下降。

paras.en: A gold Audi with manufacturer license plates was parked outside Trump's rally.
paras.zh: 一辆带有制造商牌照的金色奥迪停在特朗普集会外。

paras.en: U.S. Senator Bernie Moreno, an Ohio Republican, said late on Saturday that "with this investment, Audi will build all of their SUVs exclusively in the U.S." He said the Audi plant "would never have happened without tariffs, without common sense regulations and without eliminating California's ability to regulate fuel economy standards."
paras.zh: 美国参议员、俄亥俄州共和党人伯尼·莫雷诺周六晚间表示，“通过这项投资，奥迪将专门在美国生产所有 SUV。”他表示，如果没有关税、没有常识性法规、也没有消除加州监管燃油经济性标准的能力，奥迪工厂就永远不会建成。

paras.en: Audi sales have fallen for two consecutive years and slid 7% in the first half of 2026 as fierce competition in China and U.S. tariffs hit demand. Audi's U.S. sales are down 16% this year.
paras.zh: 由于中国激烈竞争和美国关税打击需求，奥迪销量连续两年下滑，2026年上半年下滑7%。奥迪今年在美国的销量下降了 16%。

paras.en: Audi's Neckarsulm plant in southwest Germany is one of four German Volkswagen plants that could close after 2030.
paras.zh: 奥迪位于德国西南部的内卡苏尔姆工厂是可能在 2030 年后关闭的四家德国大众工厂之一。

paras.en: In July, Japan's Toyota Motor said it would spend $3.6 billion to build a 2.5-million-square-foot (232,000-square-meter) truck assembly line at its San Antonio, Texas, manufacturing campus and shift some truck production from Mexico to the U.S. The Japanese automaker said it would complete the expansion by 2030, creating 2,000 jobs.
paras.zh: 7月，日本丰田汽车表示将斥资36亿美元在其德克萨斯州圣安东尼奥制造园区建造一条250万平方英尺（232,000平方米）的卡车装配线，并将部分卡车生产从墨西哥转移到美国。这家日本汽车制造商表示将在2030年之前完成扩建，创造2,000个就业岗位。

paras.en: Honda Motor is considering building a US assembly plant but has warned it may not unless the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement on trade is extended. Last year, South Korea's Hyundai said that if it had certainty about USMCA, it "would immediately unlock over $20 billion in new American investments."
paras.zh: 本田汽车正在考虑在美国建立一家装配厂，但警告称，除非延长美国-墨西哥-加拿大贸易协议，否则可能不会这样做。去年，韩国现代汽车表示，如果它对 USMCA 有确定性，它将“立即释放超过 200 亿美元的美国新投资”。

articles.title: This implant burns up excess blood sugar with electricity

paras.en: A new wireless implant could burn up excess sugar in the blood, letting people with type 2 diabetes live healthier lives without having to completely rely on medication.
paras.zh: 一种新的无线植入物可以燃烧血液中多余的糖分，让 2 型糖尿病患者过上更健康的生活，而不必完全依赖药物。

paras.en: Traditional drugs used for diabetes such as insulin, metformin and glucagonlike peptide 1 (GLP-1) agonists all treat the condition by effectively forcing the body to keep glucose levels under control—but these treatments are prone to side effects and many involve taking a fixed quantity of medication regularly despite blood sugar changing with mood, sleep and meals. Automated insulin pumps can adjust dosing to a patient’s blood sugar in real time, but they still deliver drugs that can linger in the body.
paras.zh: 用于治疗糖尿病的传统药物，如胰岛素、二甲双胍和胰高血糖素样肽 1 (GLP-1) 激动剂，都是通过有效地迫使身体控制血糖水平来治疗糖尿病，但这些治疗方法很容易产生副作用，而且许多治疗方法需要定期服用固定剂量的药物，尽管血糖会随着情绪、睡眠和进餐而变化。自动胰岛素泵可以根据患者的血糖实时调整剂量，但它们仍然会输送可在体内停留的药物。

paras.en: “We wanted to have a completely new principle,” says Martin Fussenegger, the study’s senior author and a bioengineer at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich. For a new study in mice, published in Science, he and his team abandoned drugs altogether by developing a below-the-skin implant that chemically eliminates glucose from the blood on its own rather than triggering the body’s own mechanisms in order to do so.
paras.zh: “我们想要一个全新的原理，”该研究的资深作者、瑞士苏黎世联邦理工学院的生物工程师 Martin Fussenegger 说。在《科学》杂志上发表的一项针对小鼠的新研究中，他和他的团队完全放弃了药物，开发了一种皮下植入物，可以通过化学方式自行消除血液中的葡萄糖，而不是触发人体自身的机制来消除葡萄糖。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The device, called ECHO, which stands for electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization, looks like a little flat rectangular chip, roughly the size of a USB stick. It contains a graphite wafer that carries an electric current, embedded with branching structures of gold nanoflakes that are studded with even smaller spheres of platinum. These structures work as a catalyst—a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being consumed in the process. The implant is operated and powered wirelessly, and when voltage is applied, the surface oxidizes glucose into an easily processed metabolite called gluconate. The mouse subjects’ bodies burned roughly a fifth of the resulting gluconate for energy, and the rest was flushed out through the kidneys.
paras.zh: 该设备名为 ECHO，代表电催化闭环健康优化，看起来像一个扁平的矩形小芯片，大约有 U 盘大小。它包含一个携带电流的石墨晶片，嵌入金纳米薄片的分支结构，这些金纳米薄片上镶嵌着更小的铂球。这些结构充当催化剂——一种加速化学反应但不会在过程中被消耗的物质。该植入物以无线方式操作和供电，当施加电压时，表面会将葡萄糖氧化成一种易于加工的代谢物，称为葡萄糖酸盐。小鼠受试者的身体燃烧了大约五分之一的葡萄糖酸盐来获取能量，其余的则通过肾脏排出体外。

paras.en: Blood carries important molecules similar to glucose such as fructose, galactose and lactose, but the implant successfully targeted glucose specifically. Fussenegger admits the researchers don’t yet know why it is so successful, although that likely relates to the particular combination of gold and platinum. “We have no functional or structural explanation for that. We did not design for it,” Fussenegger says. “The specificity is, I would say, a lucky strike.”
paras.zh: 血液携带与葡萄糖类似的重要分子，如果糖、半乳糖和乳糖，但植入物成功地专门针对葡萄糖。富森格承认，研究人员还不知道为什么它如此成功，尽管这可能与黄金和铂金的特殊组合有关。 “我们对此没有任何功能或结构解释。我们没有为此进行设计，”富塞内格说。 “我想说，这种特殊性是一次幸运的打击。”

paras.en: In diabetic mice with obesity, the implant brought blood glucose levels under control within an hour when turned on, and repeated treatment held it there for six weeks. The mice also showed reduced triglycerides—a type of fat associated with disease risk—and lower body weight.
paras.zh: 在患有肥胖症的糖尿病小鼠中，植入物在启动后一小时内就使血糖水平得到控制，并通过重复治疗将其保持在六周内。这些小鼠还表现出甘油三酯（一种与疾病风险相关的脂肪）减少和体重减轻。

paras.en: The team also tested the implant while connected via a smartphone to a commercial continuous glucose monitor, which relayed blood sugar readings that allowed the smartphone to turn the implant on and off as needed. For two weeks, this closed-loop system ran with no human involvement.
paras.zh: 该团队还测试了植入物，同时通过智能手机连接到商用连续血糖监测仪，该监测仪转发血糖读数，使智能手机可以根据需要打开和关闭植入物。这个闭环系统在无人参与的情况下运行了两周。

paras.en: Many glucose-focused implants under development rely on capsules containing engineered cells that secrete therapeutic proteins—these tend not to last because they get sealed off by scar tissue in the body. But for ECHO, the mice’s tissue showed no signs of inflammation around the implant, no scarring and no leached metal. Implants removed after six weeks still worked, and some remained active even after three months under the skin, according to the study.
paras.zh: 许多正在开发的以葡萄糖为中心的植入物依赖于含有工程细胞的胶囊，这些细胞可以分泌治疗性蛋白质——这些植入物往往不会持久，因为它们被体内的疤痕组织封闭。但对于 ECHO 来说，小鼠的组织在植入物周围没有显示出炎症迹象，没有疤痕，也没有浸出的金属。研究表明，六周后取出的植入物仍然有效，有些甚至在皮下三个月后仍然有效。

paras.en: “Six weeks of operational stability is already well beyond the current technology,” says Luisa Torsi, a chemist at the University of Bari Aldo Moro in Italy, who was not involved in the study. “The crucial next steps are to establish long-term tissue compatibility, sustained catalytic activity and safe, effective glucose removal at the scale required for human treatment.”
paras.zh: “六周的运行稳定性已经远远超出了当前技术的水平，”意大利巴里阿尔多莫罗大学的化学家路易莎·托尔西（Luisa Torsi）说道，她没有参与这项研究。 “接下来关键的步骤是建立长期的组织相容性、持续的催化活性以及以人类治疗所需的规模安全、有效地去除葡萄糖。”

paras.en: A mouse has roughly two milliliters of blood, whereas humans typically hold five liters—ECHO would need to scale up to function at that level. Fussenegger is confident about that task, however. As part of the study, the team circulated sugary fluid through a five-liter flask—a stand-in for human blood volume—and the implant cleared it just as efficiently.
paras.zh: 小鼠大约有 2 毫升血液，而人类通常有 5 升——ECHO 需要扩大规模才能在这个水平发挥作用。然而，富塞内格对这项任务充满信心。作为研究的一部分，研究小组通过一个五升烧瓶（人体血容量的替代品）循环含糖液体，植入物同样有效地清除它。

paras.en: Because the device is small and sits just under the skin, Fussenegger expects the implantation procedure in humans would require a minor incision rather than complex surgery. “If it’s possible to do this maybe every three months or up to a year, and then ‘I can forget my diabetes,’ I think people would be happy,” he says.
paras.zh: 由于该装置很小并且位于皮肤下，富森格预计人体植入过程需要一个小切口，而不是复杂的手术。 “如果有可能每三个月或最多一年这样做一次，然后‘我可以忘记我的糖尿病’，我想人们会很高兴，”他说。

articles.title: RFK, Jr., adviser Calley Means announces his resignation from the Trump administration

paras.en: Calley Means, a senior adviser to Secretary of Health and Humans Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., and a key figure in the “Make America Healthy Again” (MAHA) movement, has resigned.
paras.zh: 卡利·米恩斯 (Calley Means) 是美国卫生与公众服务部部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 (Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.) 的高级顾问，也是“让美国再次健康”(MAHA) 运动的关键人物，现已辞职。

paras.en: In a post on X, Means said he was leaving the Trump administration “with tremendous respect for President Trump and Bobby Kennedy.”
paras.zh: 在 X 上的一篇帖子中，米恩斯表示，他将“带着对特朗普总统和鲍比·肯尼迪的极大尊重”离开特朗普政府。

paras.en: “They laid out a vision of combatting the entrenched, dark forces in DC that profit from Americans getting sick,” Means wrote, touting MAHA achievements such as changing dietary guidelines, pushing forward psychedelic-based treatments and removing soda from SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) benefits, among others.
paras.zh: 米恩斯写道：“他们提出了打击华盛顿根深蒂固的黑暗势力的愿景，这些势力从美国人的患病中获利。”他还宣扬了 MAHA 的成就，例如改变饮食指南、推动基于致幻剂的治疗以及从 SNAP（补充营养援助计划）福利中取消苏打水等。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: A Department of Health and Human Services spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
paras.zh: 卫生与公众服务部发言人没有立即回应置评请求。

paras.en: Means, who has no experience as a health care professional, had previously worked in the private sector and founded the telehealth company Truemed, which works with customers to spend health savings account money on supplements and fitness equipment.
paras.zh: Means 没有医疗保健专业人士的经验，此前曾在私营部门工作，并创立了远程医疗公司 Truemed，该公司与客户合作，将健康储蓄账户的钱用于补充剂和健身器材。

paras.en: Many of Means’s views have come under fire from medical professionals, including his advocacy for drinking raw milk, which can contain harmful pathogens, opposition to fluoride in drinking water and description of COVID vaccines mandates for children as a “war crime.”
paras.zh: 米恩斯的许多观点都受到了医疗专业人士的批评，包括他提倡饮用可能含有有害病原体的生奶、反对饮用水中添加氟化物，以及将儿童接种新冠疫苗的规定描述为“战争罪”。

paras.en: Means also played a key role in connecting Kennedy with Trump before the 2024 election, at a time when the two were both vying for the Oval Office. Kennedy ultimately endorsed Trump after dropping out of the race and was appointed to lead HHS in turn.
paras.zh: 米恩斯还在 2024 年大选前将肯尼迪与特朗普联系起来，当时两人都在争夺椭圆形办公室。肯尼迪在退出竞选后最终支持特朗普，并被任命轮流领导美国卫生与公众服务部。

paras.en: Means’s sister, Casey Means, a wellness influencer and former physician, was nominated by Trump for the role of surgeon general in May 2025. But her name was withdrawn this past April amid concerns over her stance on vaccines, abortion pills and alternative medicine.
paras.zh: 米恩斯的妹妹凯西·米恩斯是一位健康影响者和前医生，于 2025 年 5 月被特朗普提名为卫生局局长。但由于人们担心她在疫苗、堕胎药和替代医学方面的立场，她的名字在今年 4 月被撤回。

articles.title: Here’s what the new Merck-Moderna mRNA cancer vaccine data actually show

paras.en: Data from Merck and Moderna’s phase 3 clinical trial for an mRNA-based skin cancer vaccine were leaked and then spread on social media on Thursday, prompting the pharmaceutical companies to release an early look at the results of the trial.
paras.zh: 默克公司和 Moderna 公司基于 mRNA 的皮肤癌疫苗的 3 期临床试验数据被泄露，并于周四在社交媒体上传播，促使制药公司发布了试验结果的早期预览。

paras.en: The results, which triggered a drop in Moderna’s stock, are positive, experts say. The findings are “really encouraging,” says Karen Knudsen, CEO of the nonprofit Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy. This kind of mRNA cancer vaccine was “fiction” 10 years ago, she says. “It was thought to be very difficult to do.”
paras.zh: 专家表示，这一结果是积极的，导致 Moderna 股价下跌。非营利性帕克癌症免疫治疗研究所首席执行官凯伦·克努森 (Karen Knudsen) 表示，这些发现“确实令人鼓舞”。她说，这种 mRNA 癌症疫苗在 10 年前还只是“虚构”。 “人们认为这很难做到。”

paras.en: As Scientific American previously reported, the Merck-Moderna clinical trial includes two treatments: a personalized mRNA-vaccine called intismeran autogene, which works by instructing the body on how to identify and fight cancer, and pembrolizumab (sold as Keytruda), a drug designed to prevent cancer from “hiding” from our immune system, according to Merck.
paras.zh: 正如《科学美国人》之前报道的那样，默克-Moderna 临床试验包括两种治疗方法：一种名为 intismeran autogene 的个性化 mRNA 疫苗，它的作用是指导身体如何识别和对抗癌症；另一种是派姆单抗（以 Keytruda 出售），据默克公司介绍，这是一种旨在防止癌症“隐藏”我们的免疫系统的药物。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The clinical trial included 1,137 cancer patients with “high-risk” melanoma, a type of skin cancer. Together, after a median period of about two years, the mRNA vaccine and pembrolizumab reduced the risk of cancer recurrence or death by 42 percent in people who used both treatments compared with those on pembrolizumab alone. On top of that, the dual treatment reduced the risks of cancer spreading to other parts of the body and of death by 38 percent over just pembrolizumab, according to Merck and Moderna.
paras.zh: 该临床试验纳入了 1,137 名患有“高风险”黑色素瘤（皮肤癌的一种）的癌症患者。经过大约两年的中位时间后，与单独使用派姆单抗的患者相比，使用两种疗法的患者中，mRNA 疫苗和派姆单抗将癌症复发或死亡的风险降低了 42%。最重要的是，据默克和 Moderna 称，与单独使用派姆单抗相比，双重治疗将癌症扩散到身体其他部位的风险和死亡风险降低了 38%。

paras.en: The findings don’t yet include overall survival, Knudsen notes. “Did people who got the vaccine live longer than people who didn’t? And what was their quality of life?” she asks. Those results are coming. But the new findings are “really, really good milestones along the way,” she says.
paras.zh: 克努森指出，研究结果尚未包括总体生存率。 “接种疫苗的人比没有接种疫苗的人活得更长吗？他们的生活质量如何？”她问。这些结果即将到来。但她说，新发现“是一路上非常非常好的里程碑”。

paras.en: The “big advance” is that fewer patients will see their cancer return, said Michael Postow, chief of the Melanoma Service at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, who helped run the trial, on a press briefing call on October 23. After melanoma is surgically removed, “taking this type of combination treatment will decrease the number of patients that ever have to deal with their melanoma coming back again in the future, and fewer patients [will] have to deal with additional radiation, surgery, other more complicated treatments in the future.”
paras.zh: 帮助开展该试验的纪念斯隆·凯特琳癌症中心黑色素瘤服务中心负责人迈克尔·波斯托 (Michael Postow) 在 10 月 23 日的新闻发布会上表示，“重大进步”是癌症复发的患者数量会减少。黑色素瘤手术切除后，“采用这种联合治疗将减少未来必须应对黑色素瘤再次复发的患者数量，并且需要在治疗期间接受额外放射、手术和其他更复杂治疗的患者数量也将减少。”未来。”

paras.en: On the same press call, Beth Ryzyk, a study participant, said that she’d started treatment for her melanoma in May 2024. The study is still blinded, so she doesn’t know if she received the placebo or the vaccine. But as of the day of the call, she feels "great,” she said.
paras.zh: 在同一次新闻发布会上，研究参与者 Beth Ryzyk 表示，她已于 2024 年 5 月开始治疗黑色素瘤。该研究仍处于盲态，因此她不知道自己是否接受了安慰剂或疫苗。但她说，从接到电话的那天起，她感觉“很棒”。

paras.en: “From the beginning, we believed mRNA technology could make it possible to develop cancer treatments uniquely matched to each patient’s tumor, Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel said in a statement. “These results reinforce our conviction that mRNA has the potential to fundamentally change how we treat cancer.”
paras.zh: Moderna 首席执行官 Stéphane Bancel 在一份声明中表示：“从一开始，我们就相信 mRNA 技术可以开发出与每位患者的肿瘤独特匹配的癌症治疗方法。这些结果增强了我们的信念，即 mRNA 有可能从根本上改变我们治疗癌症的方式。”

paras.en: And “mRNA is opening the door to a new kind of cancer treatment that can be tailored to each patient’s unique tumor. To fully realize this potential, we need a modernized regulatory approach that keeps pace with the science," said Alliance for mRNA Medicines executive director Clay Alspach in a separate statement.
paras.zh: mRNA 药物联盟执行董事 Clay Alspach 在另一份声明中表示：“mRNA 为一种新型癌症治疗打开了大门，这种治疗可以根据每位患者的独特肿瘤进行定制。为了充分发挥这一潜力，我们需要一种与科学同步的现代化监管方法。”

paras.en: “We also need continued federal investment in mRNA innovation," Alspach added. "Past government support for mRNA research—including during Operation Warp Speed—has helped propel the science forward. As the results from this Phase 3 study clearly show, now is not the time to go backward.”
paras.zh: “我们还需要联邦政府继续投资 mRNA 创新，”Alspach 补充道。 “过去政府对 mRNA 研究的支持——包括在曲速行动期间——帮助推动了科学的进步。正如这项第三阶段研究的结果清楚地表明的那样，现在不是倒退的时候。”

paras.en: The results have been accepted for publication in the New England Journal of Medicine, Merck and Moderna said. Now the companies are “engaging with regulatory authorities” to seek approval for their mRNA vaccine.
paras.zh: 默克和 Moderna 表示，该结果已被《新英格兰医学杂志》接受发表。现在，这些公司正在“与监管机构合作”，寻求其 mRNA 疫苗的批准。

paras.en: Moderna and Merck did not immediately reply to requests for comment from Scientific American.
paras.zh: Moderna 和默克公司没有立即回复《科学美国人》的置评请求。

paras.en: Editor’s Note (10/23/26): This is a breaking news story and may be updated.
paras.zh: 编者注（10/23/26）：这是一个突发新闻报道，可能会更新。

articles.title: Rule breaking by just a few people can be contagious
articles.author: Sujata Gupta

paras.en: On the long drive to my kid’s sporting event this weekend, most drivers, myself included, cruised a few miles over the speed limit. A few drivers, though, blazed past in the left lane. Mindful of safety — and police cruisers — I didn’t follow suit.
paras.zh: 本周末，在我孩子参加体育赛事的长途驾驶中，大多数司机（包括我自己）都超速行驶了几英里。不过，有几名司机在左侧车道上超车了。考虑到安全和警车，我没有效仿。

paras.en: Left unchecked though, a few bad actors can trigger social breakdown, researchers report October 21 in Proceedings of the Royal Society B. The truly deviant among us “basically take off the guardrails of the group,” says Lucas Molleman, a psychologist at the University of Amsterdam.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 10 月 21 日在《英国皇家学会学报 B》上报道称，如果不加以控制，一些不良行为者可能会引发社会崩溃。阿姆斯特丹大学心理学家卢卡斯·莫勒曼 (Lucas Molleman) 表示，我们当中真正的越轨者“基本上会脱离群体的护栏”。

paras.en: Molleman and his colleagues designed a thought experiment to show what it takes to sway people to bend or break the rules. They picked a contentious time: A week before the 2024 U.S. presidential election. The team recruited 750 U.S. participants, with roughly half identifying as Democrats and half as Republicans. The online participants watched an animated shooting star streak across a row of 100 squares and then selected which square shone the brightest.
paras.zh: 莫勒曼和他的同事设计了一个思想实验，以展示如何影响人们改变或打破规则。他们选择了一个有争议的时间：2024 年美国总统大选前一周。该团队招募了 750 名美国参与者，其中大约一半是民主党人，一半是共和党人。在线参与者观看动画流星划过一排 100 个方格，然后选择哪个方格最亮。

paras.en: Though the brightest square always appeared around the row’s middle, participants received more money for selecting squares farther to the right (the farthest-right square netted participants roughly the equivalent of $1.30). Dedicated rule followers, or those who always followed the rules, and rule breakers, existed in roughly equal numbers, with each comprising about a fifth of the larger group, initial tests showed.
paras.zh: 虽然最亮的方块总是出现在该行的中间，但参与者选择更右边的方块会获得更多的钱（最右边的方块为参与者带来的净收益大约相当于 1.30 美元）。初步测试显示，专心遵守规则的人，或者说始终遵守规则的人，与规则破坏者的数量大致相等，各占较大群体的约五分之一。

paras.en: The researchers then stirred the pot. Participants repeated the simple experiment several times while receiving information about a previous respondent, including their political affiliation and level of adherence to the rule. Rule followers rarely begot more rule followers, even when respondents belonged to the same political party, the team found.
paras.zh: 然后研究人员搅拌锅。参与者多次重复这个简单的实验，同时收到有关先前受访者的信息，包括他们的政治立场和遵守规则的程度。研究小组发现，即使受访者属于同一政党，规则追随者也很少会产生更多的规则追随者。

paras.en: The reverse held true for rule breakers, though. Receiving information that someone with the same political leanings had just disregarded the rules shifted selections rightward on average. Absent social cues, participants selected the farthest-right square roughly 23 percent of the time. That increased to almost 40 percent of the time after participants learned that a political comrade had made the most lucrative choice. Bad behavior, in other words, was contagious.
paras.zh: 不过，对于规则破坏者来说，情况恰恰相反。收到具有相同政治倾向的人无视规则的信息后，平均选择会向右移动。在缺乏社交线索的情况下，参与者大约 23% 的时间选择了最右边的方块。在参与者得知政治同志做出了最有利可图的选择后，这种情况增加到近 40%。换句话说，不良行为具有传染性。

paras.en: Most individuals’ rule-breaking levels mirrored or stayed below that of others. But just over 4 percent of individuals escalated deviant behavior beyond that of the previous respondent.
paras.zh: 大多数人的违规程度与其他人相同或低于其他人。但只有超过 4% 的人将异常行为升级，超过了之前的受访者。

paras.en: The researchers then created a computer simulation to see how those rule-breaking behaviors might play out across time. They designed a digital twin for each of the 750 participants and had the doppelgängers interact in groups of 100. In some scenarios, those few escalation-prone individuals could push everyone in the group toward wild rule breaking. But if the 100-twin selection had the same proportion of dedicated rule followers as the human experiment, overall deviance settled at a more intermediate level.
paras.zh: 然后，研究人员创建了一个计算机模拟，以了解这些违反规则的行为随着时间的推移会如何发挥作用。他们为 750 名参与者每人设计了一个数字孪生体，并让分身以 100 人为一组进行互动。在某些情况下，这几个容易升级的个体可能会促使小组中的每个人疯狂违反规则。但如果 100 名双胞胎的选择具有与人类实验相同比例的专门规则追随者，则总体偏差会稳定在更中间的水平。

paras.en: This study provides some keen insights into how humans might behave absent consequences, says behavioral economist Eugen Dimant of the University of Pennsylvania. “But that’s not how the world works.” His work suggests that to truly understand social contagion and the emergence of mobs, researchers must consider societal forces, such as punishments and social norms, that tend to keep behavior in check.
paras.zh: 宾夕法尼亚大学的行为经济学家尤金·迪曼特表示，这项研究为人类在没有后果的情况下如何表现提供了一些敏锐的见解。 “但这不是世界运转的方式。”他的工作表明，要真正理解社会传染和暴民的出现，研究人员必须考虑社会力量，例如惩罚和社会规范，这些力量往往会控制行为。

paras.en: To Molleman, though, the study’s insights into individual behaviors are key. This pared-down experiment shows how just a few bad actors can cause entire groups to spiral out of control. Such findings could underpin everything from collective speeding to peaceful protests that turn violent, he says. “This is fundamental science … Obviously reality is way more complex.”
paras.zh: 不过，对于莫勒曼来说，这项研究对个人行为的洞察是关键。这个简化的实验表明，仅仅几个坏人就可以导致整个群体失控。他说，这些发现可以为从集体超速到演变为暴力的和平抗议等一切行为提供依据。 “这是基础科学……显然现实要复杂得多。”

articles.title: What can minerals tell us about Earth’s past? This geologist is finding out
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: The minute Gabriela Farfan stepped into a small natural history museum in Madison, Wis., where she grew up, she knew she wanted to work with minerals. Farfan remembers seeing all different shapes and colors and being enthralled. “From that point forward, I knew I wanted to become a geologist someday,” she says.
paras.zh: 加布里埃拉·法尔凡 (Gabriela Farfan) 踏入她长大的威斯康星州麦迪逊市的一家小型自然历史博物馆的那一刻，她就知道自己想从事矿物研究。法尔凡记得看到各种不同的形状和颜色并被迷住了。 “从那时起，我就知道有一天我想成为一名地质学家，”她说。

paras.en: Farfan is now living her teenage dream as the curator of gems and minerals at the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C. Her specialty is biomineralization — how organisms build skeletons, corals, pearls and shells. Farfan hopes to answer questions about how they form and what stories they tell by studying crystal structures and the chemistry of minerals.
paras.zh: Farfan 现在实现了她青少年时期的梦想，成为华盛顿特区史密森尼国家自然历史博物馆的宝石和矿物馆长。她的专长是生物矿化——生物体如何构建骨骼、珊瑚、珍珠和贝壳。法尔凡希望通过研究晶体结构和矿物化学来回答有关它们如何形成以及它们讲述什么故事的问题。

paras.en: These days, she investigates signals trapped within minerals. Corals, for example, build layers of calcium carbonate mineral over time, trapping chemical signatures from the ocean. The data tell all kinds of stories — about stress, disease outbreaks and changes to ocean temperature and sea level. Farfan unlocks those tales using X-ray and Raman spectroscopies, bouncing beams off samples to see what they can tell us.
paras.zh: 这些天，她研究了矿物中捕获的信号。例如，随着时间的推移，珊瑚会形成一层层碳酸钙矿物，捕获来自海洋的化学特征。这些数据讲述了各种各样的故事——关于压力、疾病爆发以及海洋温度和海平面的变化。 Farfan 使用 X 射线和拉曼光谱解开这些故事，从样本上反射光束，看看它们能告诉我们什么。

paras.en: She hopes museum visitors will remember that the sparkly gemstones, the ones that first enamored her, are just as natural as the plants and bones in other exhibits. “Minerals are actual natural history objects,” Farfan says. “Those are actually formed by Mother Nature and it’s spectacular.”
paras.zh: 她希望博物馆参观者能够记住，最初让她着迷的闪闪发光的宝石与其他展品中的植物和骨头一样天然。 “矿物是真正的自然历史物体，”法尔凡说。 “这些实际上是由大自然形成的，非常壮观。”

articles.title: This ‘living drug’ could change the course of autoimmune disease
articles.author: Meghan Rosen

paras.en: Two months before the treatment that would change Lynn Montgomery-Haga’s life, she could barely walk down a hallway.
paras.zh: 在接受改变林恩·蒙哥马利-哈加生活的治疗之前两个月，她几乎无法在走廊上行走。

paras.en: In a test at the University of Colorado Anschutz, Montgomery-Haga struggled to walk 25 feet, often reaching out to the walls for support. Usually, the 49-year-old relied on her walker or wheelchair. “She had a very stiff, hesitant gait,” says Montgomery-Haga’s neurologist, Amanda Piquet.
paras.zh: 在科罗拉多大学安舒茨分校进行的一次测试中，蒙哥马利-哈加很难行走 25 英尺，经常伸手到墙上寻求支撑。这位 49 岁的女士通常依靠助行器或轮椅出行。 “她的步态非常僵硬、犹豫，”蒙哥马利-哈加的神经科医生阿曼达·皮奎特 (Amanda Piquet) 说。

paras.en: For about a decade, Montgomery-Haga had lived with a debilitating autoimmune disease known as stiff person syndrome. The progressive condition can lock up the body’s muscles without warning, leading to falls, broken bones, excruciating pain and difficulty moving. Singer Celine Dion, who returned to the stage in September after years of battling the disease, has said it can feel “like somebody’s strangling you.”
paras.zh: 大约十年来，蒙哥马利-哈加一直患有一种使人衰弱的自身免疫性疾病，称为僵人综合症。这种进行性的病症会在没有警告的情况下锁住身体的肌肉，导致跌倒、骨折、剧痛和行动困难。歌手席琳·迪翁 (Celine Dion) 在与这种疾病作斗争多年后于 9 月重返舞台，她说感觉“就像有人勒死你一样”。

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga’s own days were marked by dizziness, fatigue and pain. And sudden muscle spasms would send her sprawling. It was like the fainting goat videos popular on the internet, she says. “They get surprised and they fall over, and there’s nothing they can do about it.”
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加自己的日子充满了头晕、疲劳和疼痛。突然的肌肉痉挛会让她四肢瘫痪。她说，这就像互联网上流行的山羊晕倒视频。 “他们感到惊讶并摔倒，但他们对此无能为力。”

paras.en: But stiff person syndrome is no joke. It stripped Montgomery-Haga of her accounting job and her ability to drive. She couldn’t sit up in bed unless she had a safety bar to pull on. If she dropped the soap in the shower, it’d take her 10 minutes to pick it up.
paras.zh: 但僵人综合症可不是闹着玩的。这剥夺了蒙哥马利-哈加的会计工作和驾驶能力。除非有安全杆可以拉动，否则她无法在床上坐起来。如果她把肥皂掉在淋浴间里，她需要 10 分钟才能捡起来。

paras.en: Now, Montgomery-Haga hopes those struggles are finally coming to an end. That’s because a clinical trial with an experimental therapy has helped restore mobility for her — and others like her. She can stride through her living room again. She can landscape her front yard. She doesn’t have to brace herself when her dogs jump on her. And she hasn’t fallen once since the treatment. The change has been drastic, she says. “I’m just really excited about the future.”
paras.zh: 现在，蒙哥马利-哈加希望这些斗争最终能够结束。这是因为一项实验性疗法的临床试验帮助她和其他像她一样的人恢复了活动能力。她又可以大步穿过客厅了。她可以美化她的前院。当她的狗扑向她时，她不必支撑自己。自从接受治疗以来，她再也没有跌倒过一次。她说，变化是巨大的。 “我对未来感到非常兴奋。”

paras.en: The treatment, a type of CAR T cell therapy, extracts immune cells from a person’s body and engineers them to attack the very cells causing the disease. First used to fight cancer, CAR T is now also targeting a variety of autoimmune diseases. If given the green light by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Montgomery-Haga’s treatment would be the first such therapy approved for an autoimmune condition — and it would be the first approved treatment for stiff person syndrome.
paras.zh: 这种疗法是一种 CAR T 细胞疗法，从人体内提取免疫细胞，并改造它们来攻击引起疾病的细胞。 CAR T 最初用于对抗癌症，现在也用于治疗多种自身免疫性疾病。如果获得美国食品和药物管理局的批准，蒙哥马利-哈加的治疗将是第一个被批准用于自身免疫性疾病的治疗方法，并且这将是第一个被批准用于僵人综合症的治疗方法。

paras.en: Stiff person syndrome may be just the beginning, says Carl June, the University of Pennsylvania immunologist and oncologist who spearheaded CAR T cell therapy for cancer decades ago. The “living drug” could herald a new era of therapeutics for autoimmune diseases like lupus, rheumatoid arthritis and even multiple sclerosis. “It’s revolutionary to think how far things have gone,” June says.
paras.zh: 宾夕法尼亚大学免疫学家和肿瘤学家卡尔·琼 (Carl June) 表示，僵人综合症可能只是一个开始，几十年前他率先提出了 CAR T 细胞治疗癌症的方法。这种“活体药物”可能预示着狼疮、类风湿性关节炎甚至多发性硬化症等自身免疫性疾病治疗的新时代。 “想想事情已经走了多远，这是革命性的，”琼说。

paras.en: But he warns that it’s far too early to know if scientists have definitively cured stiff person syndrome. And there haven’t been enough people treated to get a good handle on all the possible side effects. “There could be long-term complications in autoimmune patients that don’t happen in our cancer patients,” he says. Other researchers urge caution. “It’s very important not to oversell it,” says Marc Scherlinger, a rheumatologist at Strasbourg University Hospital in France.
paras.zh: 但他警告说，现在判断科学家是否已经彻底治愈僵人综合症还为时过早。而且还没有足够多的人接受治疗来很好地处理所有可能的副作用。 “自身免疫患者可能会出现长期并发症，而我们的癌症患者不会发生这种情况，”他说。其他研究人员敦促谨慎行事。 “不要过度吹捧它，这一点非常重要，”法国斯特拉斯堡大学医院的风湿病学家马克·谢林格 (Marc Scherlinger) 说。

paras.en: For Piquet, one crucial question is how long the treatment will last. In Montgomery-Haga’s case, the answer seems to be at least two years. Montgomery-Haga still considers herself disabled, or “disabled-ish,” as she calls it. But when rating how she used to feel on a scale of one to 10, she’d put herself at a zero before treatment, she says. These days, she’s more like a seven.
paras.zh: 对于皮奎特来说，一个关键问题是治疗能持续多久。在蒙哥马利-哈加的例子中，答案似乎是至少两年。蒙哥马利-哈加仍然认为自己是残疾人，或者用她的话说，“有点残疾人”。但她说，当用 1 到 10 的等级来评估她过去的感受时，她在治疗前将自己的评分为零。如今，她更像是一个七岁的人了。

paras.en: What’s more, Montgomery-Haga says, “I think I’m still improving.”
paras.zh: 更重要的是，蒙哥马利-哈加说，“我认为我仍在进步。”

paras.en: There’s no single symptom that clued Montgomery-Haga in to her disease. In 2014, she started having difficulty picking things up off the floor. Then her boss asked her why she was limping — Montgomery-Haga hadn’t noticed. Her balance was off and her head felt weird, like “I was walking around in a fishbowl,” she says. It got to the point where Montgomery-Haga had difficulty crossing thresholds between rooms.
paras.zh: 没有任何单一症状表明蒙哥马利-哈加患有她的疾病。 2014年，她开始难以拾起地板上的东西。然后她的老板问她为什么一瘸一拐——蒙哥马利-哈加没有注意到。她失去了平衡，头感觉很奇怪，就像“我在鱼缸里走来走去”，她说。蒙哥马利-哈加已经很难跨过房间之间的门槛了。

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga would startle easily, prompting her body to stiffen up like a board. One time when cooking, she burned her finger, spasmed and collapsed, cracking the back of her head on the cabinets. She lay on the floor crying, but finally managed to right herself. “As soon as you hit the floor,” she says, “your muscles are like, ‘Fine,’ and you can get up again.”
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加很容易受惊，身体就会像木板一样僵硬。有一次做饭时，她的手指被烫伤，痉挛并倒下，后脑勺撞到了柜子上。她躺在地板上哭泣，但最终还是站了起来。 “一旦你落地，”她说，“你的肌肉就会说，‘很好’，你就可以再次站起来了。”

paras.en: Those unpredictable symptoms capture a slice of what life is like with stiff person syndrome, or SPS. The disease, which affects roughly 2 in 100,000 people in the United States, typically develops in a person’s 30s or 40s. It is about twice as common in women as in men.
paras.zh: 这些不可预测的症状反映了僵人综合症（SPS）的生活情况。这种疾病在美国大约每 10 万人中就有 2 人受到影响，通常在 30 多岁或 40 多岁时发病。女性的发病率约为男性的两倍。

paras.en: Scientists don’t know what sets off the disease. But they think a person’s own antibodies start attacking a neurological network that helps muscles throughout the body relax. And when those tensed muscles are in opposition, like the biceps and triceps, they start fighting one another, Piquet says. That’s when people can end up in a stuck position, leading to stiffness. But because everyone’s immune system is different, patients’ experiences with the disease can vary greatly.
paras.zh: 科学家们不知道是什么引发了这种疾病。但他们认为，一个人自身的抗体开始攻击帮助全身肌肉放松的神经网络。皮奎特说，当这些紧张的肌肉（例如二头肌和三头肌）处于对立状态时，它们就会开始互相对抗。这时人们可能会陷入困境，导致僵硬。但由于每个人的免疫系统不同，患者的疾病经历可能会有很大差异。

paras.en: For Tara Zier, a former dentist based in Maryland, SPS started with extreme neck pain, blood pressure spikes, shortness of breath and feelings of impending doom. While some people struggle with mobility, Zier’s difficulties include standing and extreme fatigue. When she holds herself upright, her muscles clamp down on her spine like it’s in a vise. “Have you ever had a charley horse in your calf?” she asks. “Imagine one in your whole body that stops you in your tracks.”
paras.zh: 塔拉·齐尔 (Tara Zier) 是马里兰州的一名前牙医，SPS 开始时伴随着颈部极度疼痛、血压飙升、呼吸急促和厄运即将来临的感觉。虽然有些人行动不便，但齐尔的困难包括站立和极度疲劳。当她直立时，她的肌肉会像虎钳一样夹紧脊柱。 “你的小腿里曾经养过查理马吗？”她问。 “想象一下你全身有一个东西让你停下来。”

paras.en: Zier and Montgomery-Haga went years before learning what was behind their symptoms. Their cases mystified doctors — Zier saw 13 specialists and visited the emergency room nine times before getting a diagnosis. When she finally found out she had SPS three years after her first symptoms, Zier says she felt validated, like medicine was confirming what she already knew: “Something’s wrong with me.”
paras.zh: 齐尔和蒙哥马利-哈加花了很多年才了解他们症状背后的原因。他们的病例让医生感到困惑——齐尔在得到诊断之前看了 13 名专家并去了急诊室 9 次。齐尔说，当她在首次出现症状三年后终于发现自己患有 SPS 时，她感到自己得到了认可，就像医学证实了她已经知道的事情一样：“我有些问题。”

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga’s 2018 diagnosis put her “over the moon,” she says. For nearly four years, she had gotten sicker and sicker — but doctors couldn’t tell her why. She felt as if they were giving up on her. With the diagnosis, Montgomery-Haga not only learned that SPS existed, she says, “I was told it’s treatable.”
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加 2018 年的诊断让她“欣喜若狂”，她说。近四年来，她的病情越来越严重，但医生却无法告诉她原因。她觉得他们好像要放弃她了。通过诊断，蒙哥马利-哈加不仅了解到 SPS 的存在，她说，“我还被告知这是可以治疗的。”

paras.en: Current treatments include muscle relaxers, anti-seizure medications and Botox injections in body parts that feel especially stiff. Although these off-label therapies can address people’s symptoms, they’re “doing nothing to treat the underlying autoimmune disease,” Piquet says. And some can come with potent side effects, like mental fog.
paras.zh: 目前的治疗方法包括肌肉松弛剂、抗癫痫药物以及在感觉特别僵硬的身体部位注射肉毒杆菌。皮奎特说，尽管这些标签外疗法可以解决人们的症状，但它们“对治疗潜在的自身免疫性疾病没有任何作用”。有些可能会带来严重的副作用，比如精神迷雾。

paras.en: Zier, who has tried multiple combinations of different meds, remembers frequently losing her train of thought. She has since tapered off all but one drug, a low dose of Valium. “The trade-off,” she says, “is pain.”
paras.zh: 齐尔尝试过不同药物的多种组合，她记得经常失去思路。此后，她逐渐减少了除一种药物（低剂量的安定）外的所有药物的用量。 “代价是，”她说，“就是痛苦。”

paras.en: People with SPS can also receive intravenous infusions of healthy antibodies, a treatment called IVIG, to decrease muscle spasms and stiffness. Montgomery-Haga found it helpful but time-consuming. She’d go to the clinic every three weeks for an infusion, which could take up to six hours.
paras.zh: 患有 SPS 的人还可以接受静脉注射健康抗体（一种称为 IVIG 的治疗方法），以减少肌肉痉挛和僵硬。蒙哥马利-哈加发现这很有帮助，但很耗时。她每三周去一次诊所输液，这可能需要长达六个小时。

paras.en: “The bottom line is there are no FDA-approved therapies for this disease,” Piquet says. Now, the one most likely to cross the finish line first is something no one would have expected even a few years ago, CAR T pioneer June says. If you told doctors that CAR T cell therapy was going to be FDA approved for an autoimmune disease, he says, “people would have laughed.”
paras.zh: “最重要的是，目前还没有 FDA 批准的治疗这种疾病的疗法，”皮奎特说。 CAR T 先驱 June 表示，现在，最有可能第一个冲过终点线的人即使在几年前也没有人预料到。他说，如果你告诉医生 CAR T 细胞疗法将获得 FDA 批准用于治疗自身免疫性疾病，“人们会笑的。”

paras.en: June may be best known for his work in cancer, but he’s been keenly following the progress in auto-immune therapy. His daughter, now in her 30s, was diagnosed with juvenile rheumatoid arthritis when she was 9 years old. For her, that’s meant over 20 years of treatment with drugs that bring a bundle of side effects, such as fatigue and risk of infections. “It would be much better to be cured,” he says.
paras.zh: 琼最出名的可能是他在癌症方面的工作，但他一直在密切关注自身免疫治疗的进展。他的女儿现年30多岁，9岁时被诊断出患有幼年类风湿性关节炎。对她来说，这意味着 20 多年的药物治疗会带来一系列副作用，例如疲劳和感染风险。 “如果能被治愈就更好了，”他说。

paras.en: In autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis, lupus and SPS, a person’s own antibodies attack tissues throughout the body, from blood vessels to cartilage to neurons. Wiping out these rogue antibodies can stop the attacks. But CAR T cell therapy doesn’t act on the antibodies themselves. It goes straight to the source, snuffing out the cellular factories that manufacture them.
paras.zh: 在类风湿性关节炎、狼疮和 SPS 等自身免疫性疾病中，人体自身的抗体会攻击全身的组织，从血管到软骨再到神经元。消灭这些流氓抗体可以阻止攻击。但 CAR T 细胞疗法并不作用于抗体本身。它直达源头，消灭制造它们的细胞工厂。

paras.en: Those antibody factories are known as B cells. To eliminate them, doctors recruit T cells, which act as the body’s security system and work together to hunt down and destroy problematic cells. In the lab, scientists fine-tune these hunters, outfitting them with a molecular homing device called a chimeric antigen receptor, or CAR. When infused back into patients’ bodies, the newly-engineered T cells can target the antibody factories directly — like a saboteur told exactly what to destroy.
paras.zh: 这些抗体工厂被称为 B 细胞。为了消除它们，医生招募 T 细胞，它们充当人体的安全系统，共同努力追捕并摧毁有问题的细胞。在实验室里，科学家们对这些猎人进行了微调，为它们配备了一种称为嵌合抗原受体（CAR）的分子归巢装置。当重新注入患者体内时，新设计的 T 细胞可以直接瞄准抗体工厂——就像破坏者确切地告诉要破坏什么一样。

paras.en: The CAR T cell therapy Lynn Montgomery-Haga received wipes out B cells, including the ones likely driving her disease. Doctors hope this therapy “resets” her immune system, getting rid of harmful B cells and letting healthy new ones take their place.
paras.zh: Lynn Montgomery-Haga 接受的 CAR T 细胞疗法消除了 B 细胞，包括可能导致她患病的细胞。医生希望这种疗法能够“重置”她的免疫系统，消除有害的 B 细胞，让健康的新细胞取而代之。

paras.en: “The secret behind CAR T cell therapy is that you completely deplete B cells in the body,” says Georg Schett, a rheumatologist at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg in Germany. Temporarily wiping out a person’s B cells lets the body replace them with fresh, unproblematic ones, Schett says. He calls it an “immune reset.”
paras.zh: “CAR T 细胞疗法背后的秘密是完全耗尽体内的 B 细胞，”德国埃尔兰根-纽伦堡弗里德里希-亚历山大大学的风湿病学家 Georg Schett 说。谢特说，暂时清除一个人的 B 细胞可以让身体用新鲜的、没有问题的 B 细胞取而代之。他称之为“免疫重置”。

paras.en: CAR T cell therapy got its start in the 2010s, when researchers used engineered T cells to target cancer. In 2017, the FDA approved the first CAR T cell therapies for two blood cancers, acute lymphoblastic leukemia and large B cell lymphoma. Soon after, scientists saw the first tantalizing hints that it might work for autoimmune diseases, too. In some cases, cancer patients with autoimmune disorders reported improvements in both conditions after treatment.
paras.zh: CAR T 细胞疗法始于 2010 年代，当时研究人员使用工程 T 细胞来靶向癌症。 2017年，FDA批准了首个CAR T细胞疗法用于治疗两种血癌：急性淋巴细胞白血病和大B细胞淋巴瘤。不久之后，科学家们看到了第一个诱人的迹象，表明它也可能对自身免疫性疾病有效。在某些情况下，患有自身免疫性疾病的癌症患者报告说，治疗后这两种情况都有所改善。

paras.en: But most researchers didn’t think it could be that easy, Schett says. After all, autoimmune diseases were driven by a complex network of cell types. How could targeting just one of them work?
paras.zh: 但大多数研究人员认为事情没那么容易，谢特说。毕竟，自身免疫性疾病是由复杂的细胞类型网络驱动的。只针对其中一个怎么可能有效呢？

paras.en: That thinking underwent a paradigm shift in 2021 when Schett and his team published the first major paper reporting a successful treatment with the therapy. The patient was a 20-year-old woman with a severe case of lupus, a complex, sometimes-fatal illness that can damage the kidneys and other organs. Within five weeks of CAR T cell therapy treatment, signs of her disease began to vanish.
paras.zh: 2021 年，当 Schett 和他的团队发表了第一篇报告该疗法成功治疗的重要论文时，这种想法发生了范式转变。患者是一名 20 岁女性，患有严重的狼疮，这是一种复杂的、有时甚至致命的疾病，会损害肾脏和其他器官。在接受 CAR T 细胞疗法治疗五周内，她的疾病迹象开始消失。

paras.en: Results like these were “unheard of,” says rheumatologist Maximilian Konig of Johns Hopkins Medicine in Baltimore. Lupus is extremely difficult to treat, and for decades, most drugs tested against it failed. No one had ever seen the kind of improvements that Schett’s patient experienced.
paras.zh: 巴尔的摩约翰·霍普金斯医学院的风湿病学家马克西米利安·科尼格说，这样的结果“闻所未闻”。狼疮极难治疗，几十年来，大多数针对狼疮的药物测试都失败了。没有人见过谢特的病人所经历的那种改善。

paras.en: After the paper came out, “everybody was talking about it,” Konig says. Today, more than five years later, the woman’s lupus hasn’t returned, Schett says. “We consider this patient cured,” he says.
paras.zh: 论文发表后，“每个人都在谈论它，”科尼格说。谢特说，五年多后的今天，这位女士的狼疮还没有复发。 “我们认为这名患者已经治愈，”他说。

paras.en: The woman’s response was no fluke. The following year, Schett’s team reported similar results in five more lupus patients. All went into remission after CAR T cell therapy.
paras.zh: 女人的反应并非侥幸。第二年，谢特的团队在另外五名狼疮患者中报告了类似的结果。 CAR T 细胞治疗后，所有患者的病情均得到缓解。

paras.en: This was the true tipping point, June says. “It’s rare, very rare, that you get such striking results.”
paras.zh: 琼说，这是真正的转折点。 “能得到如此惊人的结果，非常罕见。”

paras.en: What followed was an explosion of research around the world. Scientists are now testing CAR T cell therapy in nearly a dozen autoimmune diseases linked to harmful B cells, including lupus, rheumatoid arthritis and a connective-tissue disease known as systemic sclerosis.
paras.zh: 随之而来的是世界各地研究的爆炸式增长。科学家们目前正在测试 CAR T 细胞疗法治疗近十几种与有害 B 细胞相关的自身免疫性疾病，包括狼疮、类风湿性关节炎和一种称为系统性硬化症的结缔组织疾病。

paras.en: Kyverna, the California-based company behind the SPS trial, is also running trials for neurological autoimmune conditions including generalized myasthenia gravis and progressive multiple sclerosis, or MS.
paras.zh: Kyverna 是一家总部位于加利福尼亚州的 SPS 试验背后的公司，该公司还在针对神经系统自身免疫性疾病进行试验，包括全身性重症肌无力和进行性多发性硬化症 (MS)。

paras.en: One reason using CAR T cell therapy for neurological conditions excites researchers is because of the cells’ potential to slip past the blood-brain barrier. That means they might be able to access pockets of smoldering inflammation inaccessible to other drugs, says neurologist Rebecca Farber of Columbia University.
paras.zh: 使用 CAR T 细胞疗法治疗神经系统疾病让研究人员兴奋的原因之一是这些细胞具有穿过血脑屏障的潜力。哥伦比亚大学神经学家丽贝卡·法伯说，这意味着它们可能能够接触到其他药物无法接触到的闷烧炎症区域。

paras.en: That could be a huge help in diseases like MS, in which a person’s antibodies attack the protective sheaths around nerve cells, causing numbness, brain fog and difficulty walking. Still, Farber doubts that CAR T cell therapy could fix existing damage. “We’re not expecting it to repair the nervous system,” she says. But it’s possible the treatment could freeze the disease’s progress. Patients are already asking her team about future treatments.
paras.zh: 这可能对治疗多发性硬化症等疾病有很大帮助，在这种疾病中，人的抗体会攻击神经细胞周围的保护鞘，导致麻木、脑雾和行走困难。尽管如此，法伯仍怀疑 CAR T 细胞疗法能否修复现有损伤。 “我们并不指望它能修复神经系统，”她说。但这种治疗有可能阻止疾病的进展。患者已经向她的团队询问未来的治疗方法。

paras.en: For Piquet, who cares for roughly 100 people with SPS, Kyverna’s trial offered a compelling opportunity to help her patients. Montgomery-Haga cried when Piquet told her about the trial at one of their regular Zoom appointments. She recalls wondering, is this the treatment that “might help me be normal again?”
paras.zh: 对于负责照顾大约 100 名 SPS 患者的 Piquet 来说，Kyverna 的试验为帮助她的患者提供了一个令人信服的机会。当皮奎特在他们定期的 Zoom 约会中告诉蒙哥马利-哈加有关审判时，蒙哥马利-哈加哭了。她回忆道，她当时想，这种治疗“可能会帮助我恢复正常吗？”

paras.en: The good, the bad and the potentially ugly
paras.zh: 好的、坏的和潜在的丑陋

paras.en: Though Montgomery-Haga leapt at the chance to try Kyverna’s treatment, called miv-cel, CAR T cell therapy is no walk in the park. Before starting, doctors sit patients down to “talk about the good, the bad and the potentially ugly,” Piquet says.
paras.zh: 尽管 Montgomery-Haga 抓住了机会尝试 Kyverna 的治疗方法 miv-cel，但 CAR T 细胞疗法并不是在公园里散步。皮奎特说，在开始之前，医生会让病人坐下来“谈论好的、坏的和可能丑陋的事情”。

paras.en: That includes the rigorous prep work needed before people receive their engineered T cells. Patients must first get low-dose chemotherapy, which flushes T cells from the body and makes space for the new ones. Chemo can ambush the body with symptoms including hair thinning, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.
paras.zh: 这包括人们接受工程 T 细胞之前所需的严格准备工作。患者必须首先接受低剂量化疗，将 T 细胞从体内清除，并为新细胞腾出空间。化疗可能会给身体带来一些症状，包括头发稀疏、恶心、呕吐和腹泻。

paras.en: Treatment itself also carries risks. It destroys most B cells in the body — not just the ones that cause disease. That can lead to fever, inflammation and potentially risky infections. In Kyverna’s trial, for example, 15 percent of participants had severely low white blood cell counts after treatment. Such symptoms were expected, Piquet says, and were easily treated.
paras.zh: 治疗本身也存在风险。它会破坏体内的大多数 B 细胞，而不仅仅是导致疾病的 B 细胞。这可能会导致发烧、炎症和潜在的危险感染。例如，在 Kyverna 的试验中，15% 的参与者在治疗后白细胞计数严重偏低。皮奎特说，这种症状是预料之中的，而且很容易治疗。

paras.en: Other CAR T treatments seem to have fared far worse. In August, the pharmaceutical company Novartis paused clinical trials of its therapy, rap-cel, across a spectrum of autoimmune diseases after three patients died. Bristol Myers Squibb has also paused similar studies after some patients experienced neurological complications, according to the Wall Street Journal. Details of the incidents were slow to emerge and have set the field on edge. “It’s a tragedy,” Konig says. He calls such outcomes an important wake-up call.
paras.zh: Other CAR T treatments seem to have fared far worse.八月，诺华制药公司在三名患者死亡后暂停了其治疗多种自身免疫性疾病的疗法 rap-cel 的临床试验。据《华尔街日报》报道，在一些患者出现神经系统并发症后，百时美施贵宝也暂停了类似的研究。 Details of the incidents were slow to emerge and have set the field on edge. “这是一场悲剧，”科尼格说。 He calls such outcomes an important wake-up call.

paras.en: But red flags in one trial don’t mean all CAR T products are dangerous, Konig says. That’s because many different designs and manufacturing processes exist, and scientists can’t always predict what will make one product toxic and another safe. Kyverna’s miv-cel, for instance, has been consistently well-tolerated in the more than 100 patients treated, a spokesperson for the company says.
paras.zh: 但科尼格说，一项试验中的危险信号并不意味着所有 CAR T 产品都是危险的。这是因为存在许多不同的设计和制造工艺，科学家无法总能预测什么会使一种产品有毒而另一种产品安全。例如，该公司发言人表示，Kyverna 的 miv-cel 在 100 多名接受治疗的患者中一直表现出良好的耐受性。

paras.en: CAR T cell therapies are transformative, Konig says. “They’re going to change the field — but there are risks.”
paras.zh: Konig 说，CAR T 细胞疗法具有变革性。 “他们将改变这个领域——但也存在风险。”

paras.en: Another risk is that the once-vanquished disease will return. Doctors don’t know all the genetic and environmental conditions that trigger autoimmune disease. Some researchers wonder whether vulnerable individuals remain vulnerable, even after treatment. But because it often takes multiple insults for someone to tip into a state of disease, Scherlinger says, CAR T cell therapy could buy patients lots of time.
paras.zh: 另一个风险是曾经被战胜的疾病将会卷土重来。医生并不了解引发自身免疫性疾病的所有遗传和环境条件。一些研究人员想知道，即使在接受治疗后，脆弱的个体是否仍然脆弱。但谢林格表示，由于一个人往往需要多次受到伤害才会陷入疾病状态，因此 CAR T 细胞疗法可以为患者赢得大量时间。

paras.en: After 10 days in the hospital for her treatment, Montgomery-Haga returned to recover at home. In the following months, she started to notice some changes. It was easier getting around the house, for one. And she felt her balance and stability improving. She can now kneel down to garden and clean without the days of recovery it used to require. “I can vacuum my house,” she says. “It seems so little, but now I can vacuum!”
paras.zh: After 10 days in the hospital for her treatment, Montgomery-Haga returned to recover at home. In the following months, she started to notice some changes.一方面，在房子里走动更容易。 And she felt her balance and stability improving. She can now kneel down to garden and clean without the days of recovery it used to require. “我可以给我的房子吸尘，”她说。 “看起来很小，但现在我可以吸尘了！”

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga can even sit down “crisscross applesauce,” she says. “I couldn’t do that for, like, 10 years.”
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加甚至可以坐下来“纵横交错的苹果酱”，她说。 “我大概有 10 年都做不到这一点。”

paras.en: Four months after the treatment, Piquet’s team tested Montgomery-Haga’s walking ability. In a hallway at University of Colorado Anschutz’s research building, the team marked out 25 feet with little orange cones. At one end stood Montgomery-Haga. At the other, Piquet watched behind a video camera. This time, Montgomery-Haga’s gait was smooth and her arms were down, not hovering out into the air to catch herself if she fell. “You could see that she was walking with a lot more confidence,” Piquet says.
paras.zh: 治疗四个月后，皮奎特的团队测试了蒙哥马利-哈加的步行能力。在科罗拉多大学安舒茨分校研究大楼的走廊里，研究小组用橙色小锥体标记了 25 英尺。蒙哥马利-哈加站在一端。另一方面，皮奎特在摄像机后面观看。这一次，蒙哥马利-哈加的步态平稳，双臂垂下，不会在摔倒时悬停在空中接住自己。 “你可以看到她走路时更加自信了，”皮奎特说。

paras.en: The team saw similar results in other SPS patients. Some who had difficulty walking before treatment now wanted to run, Piquet says. “It’s incredible to just see those patients speeding down the hallway.” She remembers smiles, high fives and a sense of celebration in the air. Eight of 12 people who had used a walking aid for the initial test didn’t need one for the follow-up, Piquet reported at the American Academy of Neurology meeting in April.
paras.zh: 研究小组在其他 SPS 患者中也看到了类似的结果。皮奎特说，一些在治疗前行走困难的人现在想跑步。 “看到那些病人在走廊上疾驰，真是令人难以置信。”她记得微笑、击掌和空气中的庆祝气氛。皮奎特在 4 月份的美国神经病学学会会议上报告说，在初次测试中使用助行器的 12 人中有 8 人在后续测试中不需要助行器。

paras.en: In September, Kyverna reported the trial’s one-year results: Patients maintained mobility improvements, with a third completing their 25-foot walk about as fast as a healthy adult. Additionally, nearly all patients no longer rely on immuno-suppressive drugs to tamp down harmful immune activity. That’s good news because such drugs can bring all sorts of nasty side effects, like vomiting, bleeding and infections.
paras.zh: 9 月，Kyverna 报告了该试验的一年结果：患者的活动能力保持改善，三分之一的患者完成 25 英尺步行的速度与健康成年人的速度相当。此外，几乎所有患者都不再依赖免疫抑制药物来抑制有害的免疫活动。这是个好消息，因为此类药物会带来各种令人讨厌的副作用，如呕吐、出血和感染。

paras.en: The results with SPS are “really something to celebrate,” June says. But only time and many more treatments will reveal how safe CAR T really is, he says.
paras.zh: June 说，SPS 的成果“确实值得庆祝”。但他说，只有时间和更多的治疗才能揭示 CAR T 的真正安全性。

paras.en: That’s a concern for Zier, who says she wouldn’t feel comfortable trying the therapy at this point. Zier doesn’t know how she’d respond. She’s a single mother with two kids; even a rare side effect could disrupt her life in a way she may not be able to manage. And these days, she’s managing as well as she can. Zier is the founder and CEO of The Stiff Person Syndrome Research Foundation, which supports research for SPS treatments.
paras.zh: 这是齐尔担心的问题，她说她现在不愿意尝试这种疗法。紫儿不知道自己会作何反应。她是一位有两个孩子的单亲妈妈；即使是罕见的副作用也可能以她无法应对的方式扰乱她的生活。如今，她已经尽力做到最好了。 Zier 是僵人综合症研究基金会的创始人兼首席执行官，该基金会支持 SPS 治疗研究。

paras.en: Kyverna is in the process of submitting miv-cel for FDA approval. The company is seeking priority review and hopes the treatment might be available to patients in 2027. If SPS is the first autoimmune disease to have an FDA-approved CAR T cell therapy, myasthenia gravis could be the second, says Warner Biddle, Kyverna’s CEO. What’s more, miv-cel also appeared to improve symptoms in six patients with severe cases of rheumatoid arthritis, researchers reported in August in Nature Medicine.
paras.zh: Kyverna 正在向 FDA 提交 miv-cel 的批准。该公司正在寻求优先审查，并希望在 2027 年为患者提供该治疗方法。Kyverna 首席执行官 Warner Biddle 表示，如果 SPS 是第一个获得 FDA 批准的 CAR T 细胞疗法的自身免疫性疾病，那么重症肌无力可能是第二个。此外，研究人员在 8 月的《自然医学》杂志上报道称，miv-cel 似乎还改善了 6 名严重类风湿关节炎患者的症状。

paras.en: As for what’s next, the door is wide open. Some scientists are working to make off-the-shelf forms of CAR T that wouldn’t require personalized engineering. Others are trying to reprogram T cells directly inside people’s bodies, rather than in the lab. Still others are trying to make T cells that target only the B cells responsible for disease. In the future, doctors might use such drugs to help patients avoid the cumbersome treatment process that Montgomery-Haga endured.
paras.zh: 至于接下来的事情，大门是敞开的。一些科学家正在致力于制造不需要个性化工程的现成 CAR T 形式。其他人则试图直接在人体内而不是在实验室中对 T 细胞进行重新编程。还有一些人正在尝试制造只针对导致疾病的 B 细胞的 T 细胞。未来，医生可能会使用此类药物来帮助患者避免蒙哥马利-哈加所经历的繁琐治疗过程。

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga’s own future looks far different than what she had imagined a few years ago. In 2026, she took a trip to Washington, D.C., to see the monuments. Now she’d like to visit Paris, Scotland and Ireland, too.
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加自己的未来看起来与她几年前的想象大不相同。 2026年，她前往华盛顿特区参观了这些纪念碑。现在她也想去巴黎、苏格兰和爱尔兰。

paras.en: For so many years, Montgomery-Haga has looked at trips and activities — and even household chores — that most people take for granted, thinking, “Man, I wish I could do that,” she says. “Now I can.”
paras.zh: 多年来，蒙哥马利-哈加一直关注大多数人认为理所当然的旅行和活动，甚至家务，她说：“伙计，我希望我能做到这一点。” “现在我可以了。”

articles.title: Physicists May Have Inadvertently Built a Qubit That Can Run Backward in Time
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: In the classical Universe, the arrow of time flies one way – but in the quantum realm, where classical physics breaks down, could even time's direction be ripe for the tweaking?
paras.zh: 在经典宇宙中，时间之箭是单向飞行的——但在经典物理学崩溃的量子领域，时间的方向是否已经成熟，可以进行调整了？

paras.en: The ability to manipulate the direction of quantum evolution could offer new ways to process information – with implications especially for quantum computing.
paras.zh: 操纵量子演化方向的能力可以提供处理信息的新方法——尤其对量子计算具有影响。

paras.en: Korean physicists have demonstrated a qubit whose processes can be run backward in time… and the deliciously ironic twist is that they had to go back in time to find it.
paras.zh: 韩国物理学家已经展示了一种量子位，其过程可以向后运行……而讽刺的是，他们必须回到过去才能找到它。

paras.en: In a new preprint, physicist Tai Hyun Yoon of Korea University developed a theory describing what he calls a quantum vacuum-seeded single-photon time qubit – and showed that an experiment he and colleagues conducted in 2018 for an entirely different purpose had inadvertently already shown it in action.
paras.zh: 在一份新的预印本中，高丽大学的物理学家 Tai Hyun Yoon 提出了一种理论，描述了他所谓的量子真空种子单光子时间量子位，并表明他和同事在 2018 年为完全不同的目的进行的一项实验已经无意中展示了它的实际效果。

paras.en: The notion of a time qubit is a relatively recent one, arising in a preprint penned by physicist Yakov Bloch of Tel Aviv University, uploaded to arXiv in November 2025.
paras.zh: 时间量子位的概念是一个相对较新的概念，出现在特拉维夫大学物理学家 Yakov Bloch 撰写的预印本中，并于 2025 年 11 月上传到 arXiv。

paras.en: It's not actually a qubit that can travel backward in time; rather, as Bloch explains it, it's a quantum system that can evolve in two opposite temporal directions at once.
paras.zh: 它实际上并不是一个可以时光倒流的量子位；它只是一个量子比特。相反，正如布洛赫所解释的那样，它是一个可以同时沿两个相反的时间方向演化的量子系统。

paras.en: Imagine a clock whose hands can run both clockwise and counterclockwise simultaneously. That's roughly the idea – except that instead of turning back time itself, the qubit allows physicists to manipulate the direction in which a quantum process unfolds.
paras.zh: 想象一个时钟，它的指针可以同时顺时针和逆时针运行。大致的想法就是这样——只不过量子位不是让时间本身倒转，而是让物理学家能够操纵量子过程展开的方向。

paras.en: He proposed that this could be experimentally tested by splitting the path of a quantum particle in two, with opposing magnetic fields along the two paths, then bringing them back together. The interference pattern of their reunion could reveal how the two opposing evolutions are connected.
paras.zh: 他提出，可以通过将量子粒子的路径一分为二，沿着两条路径施加相反的磁场，然后将它们重新组合在一起来进行实验测试。他们重聚的干涉模式可以揭示这两种相反的进化是如何联系在一起的。

paras.en: As of time of writing, that idea remains solidly in the theoretical realm; but, like a quantum particle split in two, Yoon took the idea and ran with it in another direction.
paras.zh: 截至撰写本文时，这一想法仍然牢牢停留在理论领域。但是，就像量子粒子一分为二一样，尹接受了这个想法，并将其带向另一个方向。

paras.en: Instead of using magnetic fields to reverse the evolution of a spinning particle, Yoon turned to light. His approach uses two crystal sources that generate entangled photon pairs; one photon from each pair carries the single-photon qubit. The technique is called entangled nonlinear biphoton source (ENBS) interferometry.
paras.zh: 尹没有使用磁场来逆转旋转粒子的演化，而是转向了光。他的方法使用两个产生纠缠光子对的晶体源；每对中的一个光子携带单光子量子位。该技术称为纠缠非线性双光子源（ENBS）干涉测量。

paras.en: The direction of a particular quantum interaction is then controlled by adjusting the phase of the light used to generate the photons.
paras.zh: 然后通过调整用于产生光子的光的相位来控制特定量子相互作用的方向。

paras.en: Tweaking the phase by half a cycle reverses the quantum interaction – not because time itself is flowing backward, but because the mathematical process governing the interaction runs in the opposite direction.
paras.zh: 将相位调整半个周期会反转量子相互作用——不是因为时间本身在倒流，而是因为控制相互作用的数学过程朝相反的方向运行。

paras.en: In quantum mechanics, the evolution of a system over time is governed by a mathematical description called a Hamiltonian. It determines how the system's quantum state changes from one moment to the next.
paras.zh: 在量子力学中，系统随时间的演化受到称为哈密顿量的数学描述的控制。它决定了系统的量子态从一个时刻到下一个时刻如何变化。

paras.en: Reverse the sign of that Hamiltonian, and the system evolves as though time itself were running backward, retracing the changes it would otherwise undergo.
paras.zh: 反转哈密顿量的符号，系统就会不断演化，就好像时间本身在倒退一样，追溯它本来会经历的变化。

paras.en: Yoon's method doesn't reverse the entire Hamiltonian, but it does reverse the part governing the interaction he controls. This gives him two opposing directions of quantum evolution – the equivalent of a quantum clock whose hands can turn either way.
paras.zh: Yoon 的方法并没有反转整个哈密顿量，但确实反转了他控制的相互作用的部分。这给了他两个相反的量子进化方向——相当于一个指针可以向任意方向转动的量子钟。

paras.en: But two opposing directions are not in themselves a time qubit. That requires something extra – superposition, where both directions exist simultaneously.
paras.zh: 但两个相反的方向本身并不是时间量子位。这需要一些额外的东西——叠加，两个方向同时存在。

paras.en: This is where the shared laser light becomes important. Ordinarily, generating a photon pair leaves behind information that could reveal which crystal produced it. That information distinguishes the two possible paths, preventing them from producing the coherent superposition needed for a qubit.
paras.zh: 这就是共享激光变得重要的地方。通常，产生光子对会留下可以揭示是哪个晶体产生它的信息。该信息区分了两种可能的路径，防止它们产生量子位所需的相干叠加。

paras.en: But by supplying both crystals with light from the same coherent laser source, the distinguishing information can be suppressed, allowing the two opposing quantum evolutions to interfere.
paras.zh: 但是，通过向两个晶体提供来自同一相干激光源的光，可以抑制区别信息，从而允许两种相反的量子演化发生干涉。

paras.en: The result is a single-photon qubit that encodes not just two different paths, but two opposing directions of quantum evolution.
paras.zh: 结果是一个单光子量子位不仅编码两条不同的路径，而且编码两个相反的量子演化方向。

paras.en: Yoon didn't need to design and build an entirely new experiment to show this approach is feasible. Instead, he turned to measurements from experiments he and colleagues had already conducted, including one in 2018.
paras.zh: Yoon 不需要设计和构建一个全新的实验来证明这种方法是可行的。相反，他转向了他和同事已经进行的实验（包括 2018 年的一项实验）的测量结果。

paras.en: Those experiments had demonstrated the phase-dependent behavior and interference that his new theoretical framework requires. By reexamining the data he and his colleagues had already collected, Yoon showed that the apparatus could be understood as an implementation of a single-photon time qubit.
paras.zh: 这些实验证明了他的新理论框架所需的相位相关行为和干扰。通过重新检查他和同事已经收集的数据，尹表明该设备可以被理解为单光子时间量子位的实现。

paras.en: Because it uses data from older experiments to probe a new theory, it's not a perfect demonstration. However, as a proof of concept, it suggests there could be a lot to gain by pursuing it in a dedicated investigation of time qubits.
paras.zh: 因为它使用旧实验的数据来探索新理论，所以它并不是一个完美的演示。然而，作为概念证明，它表明通过对时间量子位的专门研究来追求它可能会获得很多收获。

paras.en: A more specialized experiment with tighter control over the quantum states could test the full range of operations predicted by the theory.
paras.zh: 对量子态进行更严格控制的更专业的实验可以测试该理论预测的全部操作。

paras.en: Or, as Yoon puts it, "Coupling the discrete ENBS time qubit via controlled time-frequency displacements to hardware-native Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (TF-GKP) bosonic grid states in chronocyclic phase space establishes a robust pathway toward fault-tolerant temporal quantum error correction, high-dimensional qudit processing, and tabletop simulations of relativistic quantum detector dynamics."
paras.zh: 或者，正如 Yoon 所说，“通过受控时频位移将离散 ENBS 时间量子位与时间循环相空间中的硬件原生 Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (TF-GKP) 玻色网格状态耦合，建立了一条通往容错时间量子纠错、高维量子处理和相对论量子探测器动力学桌面模拟的稳健途径。”

paras.en: The research, which has yet to be peer-reviewed, is available on arXiv.
paras.zh: 该研究尚未经过同行评审，可在 arXiv 上获取。

articles.title: Scientists May Have Discovered Why Men's Prostates Enlarge With Age
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Scientists have discovered a distinct subtype of cell in the prostate, and it could help solve the mystery of why the gland enlarges with age.
paras.zh: 科学家们在前列腺中发现了一种独特的细胞亚型，它可能有助于解开前列腺为何随着年龄增长而增大的谜团。

paras.en: This natural phenomenon is called benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), and it tends to occur in just one region of the prostate.
paras.zh: 这种自然现象称为良性前列腺增生 (BPH)，它往往只发生在前列腺的一个区域。

paras.en: But scientists still don't understand why.
paras.zh: 但科学家们仍然不明白为什么。

paras.en: Now, researchers at Johns Hopkins University have found a possible culprit hiding around the urethra.
paras.zh: 现在，约翰·霍普金斯大学的研究人员发现了可能的罪魁祸首隐藏在尿道周围。

paras.en: Using single-cell RNA sequencing, the team has identified a population of prostate cells that are particularly abundant in this region, especially in cases of BPH.
paras.zh: 通过单细胞 RNA 测序，研究小组确定了该区域特别丰富的前列腺细胞群，尤其是在 BPH 病例中。

paras.en: The findings are published in The Journal of Pathology.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《病理学杂志》上。

paras.en: "Although BPH affects millions of men worldwide, scientists still do not fully understand why it develops primarily in a region of the prostate known as the transition zone, while other regions of the gland remain relatively unaffected," explains senior author Vasan Yegnasubramanian.
paras.zh: 资深作者 Vasan Yegnasubramanian 解释说：“尽管前列腺增生症影响着全世界数百万男性，但科学家们仍然不完全明白为什么它主要发生在前列腺的一个称为过渡区的区域，而腺体的其他区域相对不受影响。”

paras.en: The transition zone is the part of the prostate that surrounds the urethra.
paras.zh: 过渡区是前列腺周围尿道的部分。

paras.en: If this area enlarges with age, it can constrict the passage, making urination slower and more sporadic.
paras.zh: 如果这个区域随着年龄的增长而扩大，它会收缩通道，使排尿更慢、更不规律。
