paras.zh: 了解有关 Litens OAD 的更多信息并找到适合您的应用的部件：

articles.title: Can R-444A Help Your Shop Lower AC Costs?
articles.author: Doug Kaufman

paras.en: Every refrigerant change brings another round of questions for shop owners. What equipment do we need? What will it cost? How much training is involved? And how does the investment translate into better service for customers?
paras.zh: 每次制冷剂的更换都会给店主带来新一轮的问题。我们需要什么设备？费用是多少？涉及多少培训？投资如何转化为为客户提供更好的服务？

paras.en: In this episode of Shop Owner Solutions, presented by Orbia Fluor & Energy Materials, we discuss another option: Klea Edge R-444A, which Orbia has positioned as an aftermarket alternative to R-1234yf.
paras.zh: 在 Orbia Fluor & Energy Materials 推出的本期店主解决方案中，我们讨论了另一种选择：Klea Edge R-444A，Orbia 将其定位为 R-1234yf 的售后替代品。

paras.en: Joining the conversation are Chuck Abbott, Orbia’s global marketing manager, and Wade Pugh, owner of Wade’s Fixit Shop. Chuck explains the product’s reported performance and cost advantages, while Wade brings the discussion into the bay with firsthand experience retrofitting vehicles at his shop.
paras.zh: 加入对话的还有 Orbia 全球营销经理 Chuck Abbott 和 Wade’s Fixit Shop 老板 Wade Pugh。查克解释了该产品所报告的性能和成本优势，而韦德则通过在他的商店改装车辆的第一手经验将讨论带入海湾。

paras.en: The conversation moves beyond refrigerant chemistry to the details that affect daily operations: equipment requirements, service time, technician preparation and the potential impact on the shop’s bottom line. They also address retrofit procedures, service fittings, labeling, cross-contamination prevention and safety considerations.
paras.zh: 讨论超越了制冷剂化学，涉及到影响日常运营的细节：设备要求、服务时间、技术人员准备以及对车间利润的潜在影响。它们还涉及改造程序、维修配件、标签、交叉污染预防和安全注意事项。

paras.en: For owners evaluating their next AC equipment purchase, or looking for additional ways to serve customers, those details are important. Understanding an alternative starts with knowing what the work actually involves.
paras.zh: 对于评估下一次购买空调设备或寻找其他方式为客户提供服务的业主来说，这些细节非常重要。了解替代方案首先要了解工作实际涉及的内容。

paras.en: Watch the episode above for a practical conversation about R-444A and what shop owners should consider before bringing it into their AC service business.
paras.zh: 观看上面的剧集，了解有关 R-444A 的实用对话，以及店主在将其引入空调服务业务之前应考虑的事项。

articles.title: NAPA Apprentice Program Builds a New Path Into the Service Bay
articles.author: NAPA

paras.en: As repair shops across the country struggle to recruit qualified technicians, the NAPA Auto Care Apprentice Program offers participating businesses a structured way to develop new talent inside their own service bays.

More than 700 NAPA Auto Care centers nationwide participate in the program, which combines technical education, hands-on experience and mentorship. Its mission is to educate and cultivate the next generation of automotive repair professionals by providing a broad learning experience that combines online and classroom training.
paras.zh: 全国 700 多个 NAPA 汽车护理中心参与了该计划，该计划结合了技术教育、实践经验和指导。其使命是通过提供结合在线和课堂培训的广泛学习经验来教育和培养下一代汽车维修专业人员。

paras.en: For shop owners, the program offers an alternative to waiting for experienced technicians to appear in an increasingly competitive labor market. A participating shop can identify someone with the right attitude and work ethic, then help that person build technical skills through a defined training path.
paras.zh: 对于店主来说，该计划提供了一种替代方案，让他们无需等待经验丰富的技术人员出现在竞争日益激烈的劳动力市场中。参与的商店可以识别具有正确态度和职业道德的人员，然后通过明确的培训路径帮助该人员培养技术技能。

paras.en: “NAPA is committed to finding solutions that address the national shortage of skilled automotive technicians,” said Jason Rainey, vice president of Auto Care. “Our apprenticeship program is one of several key NAPA initiatives that help pave the way for young people to launch long and fruitful careers in our industry.”
paras.zh: Auto Care 副总裁 Jason Rainey 表示：“NAPA 致力于寻找解决方案，解决全国熟练汽车技术人员短缺的问题。” “我们的学徒计划是 NAPA 的几项关键举措之一，有助于为年轻人在我们行业开展长期且富有成果的职业生涯铺平道路。”

paras.en: The NAPA Apprentice Program uses a nine-stage curriculum designed to give participants a broad understanding of the systems and components found on modern vehicles. Most apprentices can complete the program in two years or less.
paras.zh: NAPA 学徒计划采用九阶段课程，旨在让参与者广泛了解现代车辆上的系统和组件。大多数学徒可以在两年或更短的时间内完成该计划。

paras.en: However, the curriculum is competency-based rather than tied strictly to a calendar. Apprentices can progress through each stage at a pace that matches their learning style and demonstrated abilities. A participant who quickly masters a subject can move forward, while someone who needs additional practice can spend more time developing that competency.
paras.zh: 然而，课程是基于能力的，而不是严格与日历挂钩。学徒可以按照与他们的学习风格和能力相匹配的速度完成每个阶段。快速掌握某一主题的参与者可以继续前进，而需要额外练习的参与者可以花更多时间来发展该能力。

paras.en: Training is 100% technical and is delivered through several formats:
paras.zh: 培训 100% 是技术性的，并通过多种形式提供：

paras.en: - Classroom training videos exclusive to the Apprentice Program provide in-depth instruction from experienced master technicians.
paras.zh: - 学徒计划独有的课堂培训视频提供经验丰富的技术大师的深入指导。

paras.en: - NAPA Autotech classes offer instructor-led training taught by experienced ASE Master Certified instructors.
paras.zh: - NAPA Autotech 课程提供由经验丰富的 ASE 大师认证讲师授课的讲师指导培训。

paras.en: - Autotech eLearning provides web-based instruction targeting specific systems, procedures and diagnostic topics.
paras.zh: - Autotech eLearning 提供针对特定系统、程序和诊断主题的基于网络的指导。

paras.en: - Hands-on training allows apprentices to apply what they have learned while working in the shop under the guidance of a mentor.
paras.zh: - 实践培训允许学徒在导师的指导下在车间工作时运用所学知识。

paras.en: This combination helps connect classroom theory with real repairs. Apprentices do not just learn how a component operates; they also gain experience inspecting, testing and servicing that component on vehicles.
paras.zh: 这种结合有助于将课堂理论与实际维修联系起来。学徒不仅要学习组件的工作原理，还要学习组件的工作原理。他们还获得了检查、测试和维修车辆部件的经验。

paras.en: The curriculum will continue to evolve as vehicle technology and industry standards change. Planned enhancements include updated training modules and specialized certification options covering emerging service areas, giving apprentices additional opportunities for career advancement.
paras.zh: 随着车辆技术和行业标准的变化，课程将不断发展。计划的增强功能包括更新的培训模块和涵盖新兴服务领域的专业认证选项，为学徒提供更多的职业发展机会。

paras.en: Apprentices earn the work experience requirement for three Automotive Service Excellence certifications as they advance through the program: Maintenance and Light Repair (G1), Suspension and Steering (A4), and Brakes (A5). They also gain the practical know-how to pass the EPA Section 609 refrigerant recovery and recycling credential test administered through ASE.
paras.zh: 学徒在完成该计划时将获得三项卓越汽车服务认证的工作经验要求：维护和轻型维修 (G1)、悬架和转向 (A4) 以及制动器 (A5)。他们还获得了通过 ASE 管理的 EPA 第 609 节制冷剂回收和再循环证书测试的实用知识。

paras.en: That distinction is important: G1, A4 and A5 are ASE professional certifications, while Section 609 is an EPA-required credential for technicians who service motor-vehicle air-conditioning systems. Together, these credentials provide outside validation of the knowledge and skills developed during the apprenticeship.
paras.zh: 这种区别很重要：G1、A4 和 A5 是 ASE 专业认证，而第 609 条是 EPA 要求的维修机动车辆空调系统的技术人员的证书。这些证书共同为学徒期间开发的知识和技能提供了外部验证。

paras.en: Because the program is registered with the U.S. Department of Labor, graduates also finish with a nationally recognized journey-level credential in automotive repair. This gives apprentices evidence of completing a structured combination of education and supervised on-the-job training.
paras.zh: 由于该项目已在美国劳工部注册，因此毕业生还可以获得全国认可的汽车维修旅程级证书。这为学徒提供了完成教育和监督在职培训的结构化组合的证据。

paras.en: The program provides the curriculum and training materials, but its success inside a repair facility depends heavily on the shop’s involvement. An apprentice needs an experienced technician who can explain procedures, demonstrate good work habits, supervise repairs and provide constructive feedback.
paras.zh: 该计划提供课程和培训材料，但其在维修厂内的成功在很大程度上取决于商店的参与。学徒需要经验丰富的技术人员来解释程序、展示良好的工作习惯、监督维修并提供建设性反馈。

paras.en: “We need their mentorship, their participation,” said Hannah Klausman, account marketing manager for Auto Care. “We want to support them by providing the materials for their technicians to go through this program, but we need their buy-in by having them provide a mentor and really put their time into taking a chance on these new technicians.”
paras.zh: “我们需要他们的指导和参与，”汽车护理公司客户营销经理汉娜·克劳斯曼 (Hannah Klausman) 说。 “我们希望通过为他们的技术人员提供完成该计划的材料来支持他们，但我们需要他们的支持，让他们提供导师，并真正投入时间来为这些新技术人员提供机会。”

paras.en: For a shop owner, that requires a real commitment. Mentoring can temporarily affect the productivity of an experienced technician, especially during an apprentice’s first months. The potential return is a technician trained around the shop’s procedures, quality standards and culture.
paras.zh: 对于店主来说，这需要真正的承诺。指导可能会暂时影响经验丰富的技术人员的工作效率，尤其是在学徒的头几个月。潜在的回报是一名接受过工厂程序、质量标准和文化培训的技术人员。

paras.en: The program can also create a clearer career ladder. Instead of hiring someone as an entry-level employee with no defined next step, a shop can show the apprentice how training, demonstrated competencies and certifications lead to greater responsibilities.
paras.zh: 该计划还可以创建更清晰的职业阶梯。商店可以向学徒展示培训、展示的能力和认证如何带来更大的责任，而不是雇用某人作为没有明确下一步的入门级员工。

paras.en: “The success of the apprentice program is a reflection not only of the investment NAPA has made but also of its collaboration with Auto Care centers across the country,” said Ryan Ouellette, director of strategic accounts at NAPA. “We are committed to developing future professionals at NAPA, and we look forward to continuing to educate and support the talent in the industry.”
paras.zh: NAPA 战略客户总监 Ryan Ouellette 表示：“学徒计划的成功不仅反映了 NAPA 的投资，也反映了其与全国各地汽车护理中心的合作。” “我们致力于在 NAPA 培养未来的专业人士，我们期待继续教育和支持该行业的人才。”

paras.en: Applicants must be at least 17 years old. Applicants who are 17 require written parental consent, and there is no maximum age.
paras.zh: 申请人必须年满 17 岁。年满 17 岁的申请人需要获得父母的书面同意，并且没有最高年龄限制。

paras.en: Previous professional repair experience is not the program’s defining qualification. Shops should look for candidates who have a positive attitude, arrive ready to work and take initiative beyond their assigned tasks.
paras.zh: 以前的专业维修经验并不是该计划的定义资格。商店应该寻找态度积极、做好工作准备、主动超越分配任务的候选人。

paras.en: Successful apprentices must also be able to build relationships. Automotive repair is increasingly collaborative, particularly when diagnostic information, specialized equipment and technical knowledge must be shared among technicians. An apprentice must be willing to ask questions, accept coaching and learn from the people around them.
paras.zh: 成功的学徒还必须能够建立关系。汽车维修的协作性日益增强，特别是当技术人员必须共享诊断信息、专业设备和技术知识时。学徒必须愿意提出问题、接受指导并向周围的人学习。

paras.en: Most importantly, candidates need to embrace continuous learning. Vehicle technology does not stand still, and neither can a technician’s education.
paras.zh: 最重要的是，候选人需要接受持续学习。汽车技术不会停滞不前，技术人员的教育也不会停滞不前。

paras.en: For aspiring technicians, the program provides an opportunity to learn the trade without taking on the expense of a traditional trade-school program. Apprentices receive a paycheck while learning in an operating repair facility, and the training itself is provided at no cost to the participant.
paras.zh: 对于有抱负的技术人员来说，该计划提供了学习该行业的机会，而无需承担传统职业学校计划的费用。学徒在运营的维修设施中学习时可以获得薪水，并且培训本身是免费向参与者提供的。

paras.en: Additional information about the program is available at NAPA Auto Care Training.
paras.zh: 有关该计划的更多信息，请访问 NAPA 汽车护理培训。

paras.en: Sidebar: Addressing the Cost of a Technician’s First Tools
paras.zh: 侧边栏：解决技术人员第一个工具的成本问题

paras.en: Tools represent one of the largest entry barriers for a new automotive technician. Even a basic professional set can require a substantial investment before the technician earns a full professional wage.
paras.zh: 工具是新汽车技术人员最大的进入障碍之一。即使是基本的专业设置也可能需要大量投资才能使技术人员获得全额专业工资。

paras.en: To help address that barrier, Carlyle Tools developed an Apprentice Set containing professional-quality tools considered essential for a new technician’s career. NAPA Auto Care makes the exclusive set, which has a stated retail value of $6,566, available for participating Auto Care centers to purchase for their apprentices.
paras.zh: 为了帮助解决这一障碍，凯雷工具开发了一套学徒套装，其中包含被认为对新技术人员职业生涯至关重要的专业品质工具。 NAPA Auto Care 制作了这套独家套装，标称零售价为 6,566 美元，可供参与的汽车护理中心为学徒购买。

paras.en: Providing or helping finance an appropriate starter set can make a shop’s apprenticeship opportunity more attractive. It also helps ensure that the apprentice begins with tools capable of withstanding daily professional use.
paras.zh: 提供或帮助资助合适的入门套件可以使商店的学徒机会更具吸引力。它还有助于确保学徒从能够承受日常专业使用的工具开始。

articles.title: Hella Launches Commercial Vehicle Brake Pads
articles.author: Alex Crissey

paras.en: Hella Aftermarket is introducing brake pads for trucks, buses, and trailers, the company’s first offering in the commercial vehicle sector. The products are now available worldwide.
paras.zh: 海拉售后市场正在推出用于卡车、公共汽车和拖车的刹车片，这是该公司在商用车领域的首款产品。该产品现已在全球范围内销售。

paras.en: “We are starting with brake pads for trucks, buses, and trailers and will gradually expand the range,” says Dr. Marcel Wiedmann, head of the global aftermarket business at Forvia Hella. “Building on our established brake offering for passenger cars, we are now transferring our expertise to the commercial vehicle sector.”
Hella is launching an initial portfolio of 58 references, covering a range of applications and model variants, the company said.
paras.zh: 该公司表示，海拉正在推出包含 58 种型号的初始产品组合，涵盖一系列应用和型号变体。

paras.en: The new program is designed for the high thermal and mechanical loads in heavy-duty applications. Each brake lining features matched friction materials to support braking performance, service life, and comfort in daily operation. Where necessary, linings are supplied with application-specific accessories.
paras.zh: 新程序专为重型应用中的高热负荷和机械负荷而设计。每个制动衬片均采用匹配的摩擦材料，以支持制动性能、使用寿命和日常操作的舒适度。如有必要，衬里会配备特定于应用的配件。

paras.en: All brake pads are tested and certified according to international safety and quality standards, including ECE R90.

articles.title: How Simplification Can Create New Capacity for Growth
articles.author: Darcy Curran

paras.en: In the automotive aftermarket, growth is often associated with adding more: more products, more inventory, more suppliers and more resources. However, adding more doesn’t always lead to growth. In fact, adding more can introduce unnecessary complexity, making growth more difficult. The most successful businesses understand where they create the greatest value and have the discipline to direct resources toward those priorities.

No business can excel at everything. The most important strategic decision is often determining what not to do. Companies should first define what they want to be known for and how they can deliver distinctive value to customers. That requires discipline: investing in the right areas, focusing on the highest priorities, and stopping work that no longer advances the strategy.
paras.zh: 没有哪个企业能够在所有方面都表现出色。最重要的战略决策通常是确定不做什么。公司应该首先定义他们希望以什么闻名，以及如何为客户提供独特的价值。这需要纪律：投资于正确的领域，专注于最优先的事项，并停止不再推进战略的工作。

paras.en: Without this focus, complexity can surface quickly, and companies can wind up working too hard on the wrong things. The real cost isn’t limited to the time or dollars spent managing the complexity. More importantly, it includes potential growth opportunities missed because resources are not directed correctly.
paras.zh: 如果没有这种关注，复杂性就会很快显现出来，公司可能会在错误的事情上过度努力。真正的成本并不限于管理复杂性所花费的时间或金钱。更重要的是，它包括因资源分配不正确而错失的潜在增长机会。

paras.en: Inventory management is one area where this can be seen. Healthy inventory turns consistently for suppliers and distributors, whereas chronically slow-moving inventory can signal that resources are not creating enough value for customers. Even inventory that isn’t moving still requires dollars to acquire, manage, store and move through the operation, and these costs can add up quickly, especially when the product isn’t generating meaningful sales.

As an important proactive action, suppliers and distributors should consistently review inventory investment and turns to help identify which products are creating value and where resources can be better focused to help drive growth.

The purchase price is easy to measure, and too often, businesses try to sell for the most and buy for the least. But greater value can come from understanding what partners need and where their challenges exist.

For distributors, there’s also value in building deeper relationships with a focused group of suppliers. During periods of supply disruption or elevated demand, manufacturers and other suppliers naturally prioritize their most important customers. These relationships create opportunities to support each other’s businesses better while establishing mutual trust and confidence.

In one supplier relationship, we learned a partner was looking to borrow money to fund an expansion. We had already planned to extend our contract, but by executing the agreement earlier, we gave our partner longer-term, predictable business, reducing their risk to their lender and allowing them to borrow at a lower rate. This early extension allowed both sides to get what they needed without simply negotiating over another percentage point on price.
paras.zh: 在一个供应商关系中，我们了解到一位合作伙伴正在寻求借钱来资助扩张。我们本来已经计划延长合同，但通过更早地执行协议，我们为合作伙伴提供了长期、可预测的业务，降低了他们对贷方的风险，并允许他们以较低的利率借款。这种早期的延期使双方能够得到他们所需要的东西，而无需简单地就价格再进行一个百分点的谈判。

paras.en: The critical learning from this example is the importance of building relationships that are strategic rather than simply transactional. The most important question is: How can we change the way we do business to benefit both sides beyond the purchase order’s value? When distributors and suppliers understand each other’s businesses well enough to answer this question, the relationship can become stronger and create better economics for both sides.

Simplification also extends to how distributors serve their customers. By providing more flexibility in terms of how customers purchase and receive products, distributors can help customers manage their inventory more efficiently while maximizing their dollars and warehouse space.

Consider the difference between buying a case and a pallet: rather than putting significantly more cash into inventory up front, smaller quantities and more frequent replenishment can help align inventory more closely with demand.
paras.zh: 考虑一下购买箱子和托盘之间的区别：与其预先在库存中投入大量现金，不如减少数量和更频繁的补货，这样可以帮助库存更紧密地满足需求。

paras.en: That same principle can extend across the broader supplier relationship. When customers can access more of what they need in smaller quantities and combine categories into fewer shipments, they can simplify ordering and receiving, turn inventory faster and manage working capital and space more effectively.

Delivering that value also requires distributors to make smart decisions behind the scenes, specifically where distribution centers are located, how products move through them, and how far they travel to customers. All these decisions affect cost and reliability, specifically when distributing heavy, low-cost products. By adopting a more strategically positioned distribution network, distributors can reduce costs and improve service without increasing customer charges.
paras.zh: 提供这种价值还需要分销商在幕后做出明智的决策，特别是分销中心的位置、产品如何通过这些中心以及运输到客户手中的距离。所有这些决策都会影响成本和可靠性，特别是在分销重型、低成本产品时。通过采用更具战略定位的分销网络，分销商可以降低成本并改善服务，而无需增加客户费用。

paras.en: For Highline Warren, we start with a simple question: What do we want to be known for? We want customers to know that they can rely on us to deliver products on time and in full. Consistently delivering on those priorities builds credibility and can make a supplier more integral to the customer’s process, turning focus into a foundation for growth.

Understanding where a business creates value can also help identify its next growth opportunity. For suppliers and distributors, one of the easiest, fastest and most economical ways to grow is to sell existing products to existing customers. The relationship is already established, the supplier understands the customer, and the customer already knows the value the supplier provides. From there, a business should look at the broader market and consider how products or categories it already carries can help address another need.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: For example, a retailer may buy several product categories from one supplier while sourcing other products elsewhere, even though the same supplier already carries those products. The overlap creates an opportunity to grow by leveraging existing products and capabilities.

Growth frequently happens in concentric circles: first by strengthening existing relationships, then by expanding into adjacent opportunities that align with proven capabilities. Businesses that consistently deliver value earn the right to broaden those relationships over time.

Simplification isn’t simply about doing less. It is about being more deliberate and strategic about where a business puts its time, attention and resources, focusing on the areas that can drive meaningful growth.
paras.zh: 简化不仅仅是减少工作量。它是指对企业将时间、注意力和资源投入到何处更加深思熟虑和更具战略性，重点关注能够推动有意义增长的领域。

paras.en: Growth isn’t always about adding more; often, it comes from getting more from the products, capabilities and relationships a business has already established. Businesses disciplined enough to focus on this approach are better positioned to support customer needs, further strengthen relationships and create opportunities for mutual success.

articles.title: Why were the Nazca Lines built?
articles.author: Owen Jarus

paras.en: The Nazca Lines are the most famous geoglyphs in the world. Dating back around 2,000 years and reaching a combined length of more than 800 miles (1,300 kilometers), they depict a variety of motifs, including humans, animals, geometric shapes, plants and flowers. These designs were constructed on the arid hills and valleys of coastal Peru by the Nazca people between 200 B.C. and A.D. 500, long before writing was used in the region.
It's not clear exactly how many Nazca Lines there are, but they number in the thousands, with new geoglyphs continuing to be discovered with the help of AI.

Scientists have been debating this question since the lines were first formally investigated in the early 20th century. Although the definite answer remains unknown, experts have proposed various reasons for the famous geoglyphs.

There "are many ideas out there about their function and meaning," Ana Nieves, a professor of art history at Northeastern Illinois University, told Live Science in an email. "If you look at the area's geoglyphs closely, though, there are different styles of geoglyphs, some are relatively larger and some smaller, some are on hillsides while some are on the pampas. It is not likely that a single explanation would apply to all."
A vast array of theories for the lines' uses have been proposed over the years, with the most outlandish of these suggesting that they were sites for aliens to land spaceships.
More grounded theories link the lines to cultural and religious practices.
Feed your curiosity with an exclusive mystery every week, solved with science and delivered direct to your inbox before it's seen anywhere else.

"The question of why the geoglyphs exist is difficult to answer, given that we lack any type of preserved oral or written testimony," Karsten Lambers, an art history professor at the University of Augsburg in Germany, wrote in an essay published in the book "Los geoglifos: imágenes y escenarios en el desierto de Nazca y Palpa [The Geoglyphs: images and settings in the desert of Nazca and Palpa]" (University of Augsburg, 2017). It's possible that the uses for the geoglyphs changed over time, he added.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: One suggestion is that they were initially used to mark routes for travelers and caravans and later became places for gathering and feasting.

In a 2026 study, researchers noted that some of the earlier Nazca geoglyphs were constructed on hillsides, seem to be located on trails, and "were visible from considerable distances." This means the geoglyphs may have been used to mark travel routes and indicate areas that were good for temporary camps. The team suggested that the markings became places for gathering and feasting.

Another idea is that the geoglyphs were used to match astronomical alignments to serve as a kind of calendar. In December 1941, historian Paul Kosok examined the lines and determined that they had astronomical alignments. Mathematician Maria Reiche followed up on Kosok's work, examining the Nazca Lines for more than 40 years to identify many geoglyphs she believed have an astronomical relationship to various celestial bodies, a research team noted in a 2021 paper. Yet after analyzing the geoglyphs, the modern-day team found that only a relatively small number had a possible alignment to a star or solar event such as a solstice.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: "The results suggest that the geoglyphs, as a whole, certainly cannot be interpreted as a calendar system," the team wrote. However, this doesn't discredit the idea that the Nazca Lines had an astronomical significance, Christiane Richter, a researcher at the University of Applied Sciences in Germany and first author of the 2021 paper, told Live Science in an email.

Since the paper's publication, Richter and her team's research has indicated that around 8% of the geoglyphs have some form of lunar alignment. It is "highly probable that celestial bodies played a role in the creation of the drawings," Richter said in an email.

Offerings such as ceramics, crabs, corn and earrings made from Spondylus shells (a genus of bivalves known as thorny oysters) were also placed on low rock platforms near some of the geoglyphs, especially those shaped like trapezoids, Lambers noted in his paper. Spondylus shells are normally found farther north, in Ecuador, but during El Niño events, they can appear farther south, in Peru. These shells, alongside crabs and corn, tend to be associated with water and fertility, Lambers noted.

Another idea is that the geoglyphs themselves may have been used for ritual processions. Some of the geoglyphs are made with a single, uninterrupted line," Nieves said. "Those are the ones that would lend themselves for processions since people could walk them in a single file."
paras.zh: 另一个想法是，这些地质符号本身可能被用于仪式游行。有些地理符号是用一条不间断的线制成的，”尼维斯说。“这些符号适合游行，因为人们可以排成一列行走。”

paras.en: Some of the activities at the Nazca Lines may have helped foster a sense of community and equality, said Darryl Wilkinson, a professor of religion at Dartmouth University who has written about the geoglyphs. For instance, "walking the lines was a group activity, and participating in such processions would have likely created a feeling of community among those involved," Wilkinson told Live Science in an email. "I interpret the Nasca lines as geared towards the realization of a relatively more equal expression of community."
paras.zh: 达特茅斯大学宗教学教授达里尔·威尔金森（Darryl Wilkinson）曾撰写过有关地画的文章，他说，纳斯卡线的一些活动可能有助于培养社区意识和平等感。例如，威尔金森在一封电子邮件中告诉《生活科学》，“排队是一项集体活动，参加这样的游行很可能会在参与者之间产生一种社区感。” “我将纳斯卡线条解释为旨在实现相对更平等的社区表达。”

paras.en: Whatever the reasons for their construction the Nazca Lines are awe inspiring today. Lambers wrote in his essay that the Nazca people who built them "succeeded in transforming one of the driest deserts in the world, over the course of many centuries, to serve the region’s inhabitants as an expression of their cultural ideas and a setting for their social activities."

Owen Jarus is a regular contributor to Live Science who writes about archaeology and humans' past. He has also written for The Independent (UK), The Canadian Press (CP) and The Associated Press (AP), among others. Owen has a bachelor of arts degree from the University of Toronto and a journalism degree from Ryerson University.

articles.title: Watch the full 'Hunter's Moon' rise next to Saturn this weekend
articles.author: Jamie Carter

paras.en: October's full "Hunter's Moon" is about to rise, and skywatchers will get two great chances to see it appear on the eastern horizon around sunset.

Although it officially turns full at 12:11 a.m. EDT on Monday (Oct. 26), the Hunter's Moon will appear almost perfectly full as it rises on both Sunday (Oct. 25) and Monday evenings, giving skywatchers two opportunities to observe it.

October's full moon is nicknamed the Hunter's Moon because it was traditionally a signal for hunters to prepare for the coming cold winter by hunting, slaughtering and preserving meat, according to Time and Date. That's an Anglo-Saxon name; Native American names for October's full moon include the Drying Rice Moon, the Falling Leaves Moon and the Freezing Moon.

The first chance to see the Hunter's Moon comes just before sunset on Sunday, when the almost-full moon will rise in the east. The second opportunity comes on Monday, when the moon — still essentially 100% illuminated — will again rise just after sunset. Because it will be in a slightly darker sky, Monday's moonrise will likely be more dramatic.
As it rises Sunday, the moon will appear in the constellation Aries, and Saturn will be to its upper right. On Monday, it will rise above the Pleiades open cluster (M45).

For the best view on either evening, find somewhere with a clear view low to the eastern horizon and be in position shortly before moonrise where you are. An elevated viewpoint, open field or coastline is ideal because buildings, trees and hills can delay the moment the moon becomes visible.
Although the full moon will look magnificent with the naked eye, a backyard telescope or good stargazing binoculars can help you zoom in on various lunar features.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

The Hunter's Moon may appear unusually large thanks to the "moon illusion," which makes the moon seem bigger when it's seen beside familiar objects, such as trees and buildings, near the horizon. The illusion stems from the fallacies of how our brains use distance to perceive size.

October's Hunter's Moon isn't a supermoon, but it comes immediately before a notable sequence of four consecutive supermoons. The first will be the next full moon, the Beaver Moon, on Nov. 24, followed by full moons in December, January and February. A supermoon occurs when a full moon happens while the moon is relatively close to Earth in its slightly elliptical orbit, making it appear somewhat larger and brighter than average.
How much do you know about the moon? Test your lunar smarts with our moon quiz!

Jamie Carter is a Cardiff, U.K.-based freelance science journalist and a regular contributor to Live Science. He is the author of A Stargazing Program For Beginners and co-author of The Eclipse Effect, and leads international stargazing and eclipse-chasing tours. His work appears regularly in Space.com, Forbes, New Scientist, BBC Sky at Night, Sky & Telescope, and other major science and astronomy publications. He is also the editor of WhenIsTheNextEclipse.com.

articles.title: AI giants are one big mistake away from catastrophe. They could learn a lot from the nuclear industry.
articles.author: Akhil Bhardwaj

paras.en: The largest artificial intelligence (AI) firms increasingly understand that they are hostages of one another. If one firm pushes ahead recklessly, others may feel compelled to follow. If one deploys a dangerous model without adequate safeguards, others may see it as a green light to do the same.

The debate over AI has centered on what governments should do to regulate this frontier technology. That remains essential. But a more immediate question is emerging: Can the companies building these powerful systems take action independently before they lose credibility and suffer legal consequences?

That question no longer looks theoretical and is being recognized as an urgent challenge. We've already seen AI firms lose control of their models — for example, in Australia, a rogue AI hacked a government healthcare website. If we are not careful, it's only a matter of time before one of these incidents causes large-scale, real-world harm, like shutting down an electricity grid or municipal water system, or a mass misdiagnosis in a health system. If this trend continues, the entire industry could become tarnished.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: But there is a blueprint for self-regulation in a risky business: the nuclear industry, which has built up layers of oversight, controls and self-scrutiny over decades.

Frontier AI may require something similar: private regulation among competitors that do not trust one another but have a mutual interest in preventing outcomes that could damage them all. This does not appeal to the better angels of human nature — it's self-preservation for the industry itself.

There is a historical precedent for this kind of arrangement. The nuclear sector did not become safe because every actor suddenly became benevolent. It became safer through a layered system of peer scrutiny, technical standards, information-sharing and external oversight. International organizations such as the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), which was established in 1957, emerged to coordinate monitoring and verification, while national regulators and industry bodies gradually built professional norms around catastrophic risk.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The result was not perfect safety, as the Chernobyl disaster in 1986 clearly attests. But nuclear governance architecture is designed around the recognition that in high-risk technological systems, one actor's failure can become everyone's problem. This was seen following Chernobyl: global nuclear safety increased significantly after the disaster, with upgrades to reactor designs, improved training and international monitoring networks.

And this movement to self-regulation also occurred in the U.S. nuclear sector, following the Three-Mile Island nuclear accident near Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, in 1979. The reactor suffered a partial meltdown after a relatively minor cooling malfunction. Investigations later revealed design flaws in instruments and alarms, along with inadequate emergency response training, were the root cause of the incident.

The event nearly killed the nuclear energy industry in the U.S., causing public support to fall from a record high of 69% in 1977 to 46%t in 1979. The entire industry suffered because of failures at one facility. In response, the U.S. nuclear industry established the Institute of Nuclear Power Operations (INPO) in December 1979 to improve operational safety.

The analogy to AI should not be overstated. Nuclear materials are easier to count than algorithms, and nuclear facilities are harder to hide than model weights. The outcomes of a catastrophic AI blunder are also less existential, although its use in weapon systems is not without risk. In September, an AI hallucination almost led to the U.S. intercepting a Chinese ship suspected of carrying nuclear material to Iran.

Yet the comparison remains useful because the core governance problem is similar. In both cases, competitors operate in an environment where the downside risk of unchecked rivalry is borne by society while the upside is private gain for these firms. The challenge is to create institutions that make restraint the rational default — even when no actor fully trusts the others, and the inner workings of the industry are not readily visible to outsiders.

For AI, that could mean reciprocal evaluation of frontier models before deployment, secure mechanisms for sharing safety information, agreed red lines around certain capabilities, and independent third parties empowered to audit compliance. Such mechanisms would not replace government regulation. They would instead serve as an intermediate layer: stronger than voluntary ethics statements but more adaptive and technically informed than legislation alone can often be in fast-moving domains. The state would act as a background enforcer.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: AI executives appear willing to look for solutions too, with Elon Musk recently suggesting a peer-review system before advanced model release, and Demis Hassabis, co-founder and chair of Google DeepMind, putting forward a framework for an AI Standards Body, similar to the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority.

Skeptics will object, with reason, that industry-led governance can become cartel behavior or public-relations theater. Companies may use "safety" language to entrench incumbency, slow rivals or deflect binding regulation. Those are real dangers. The lesson from nuclear history is not that private coordination works automatically. It is that private coordination works only when nested inside a broader system of transparency, verification and public authority. Without those elements, private regulation becomes little more than trust-me rhetoric.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Still, dismissing private regulation altogether would be a mistake. Governments do not yet possess the technical capacity, speed or international alignment needed to oversee frontier AI on their own. And if the leading labs already see themselves as bound together by shared exposure to catastrophic risk, that recognition can become the basis for institutional design. The question is how to turn mutual fear into durable rules.
- 'We're not a competitor to fusion. We are fusion': Inside the race to harness unlimited solar power in space
- 'Autonomy always begins with something a human hands it': Who's responsible when an AI agent goes rogue?
- We're not about to awaken an evil digital god — AI is far more likely to end in a great disappointment

That is where the nuclear analogy is most powerful. It reminds us that industries facing existential hazards do not need perfect trust in order to cooperate. They need mechanisms that make cooperation preferable to defection. In practice, that means inspections, peer review, incident reporting, professional norms and a state-backed enforcement perimeter. AI governance is often discussed as if the only choices were laissez-faire innovation or heavy-handed state control. History suggests a third path: structured private coordination under public shadow.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The real opportunity, then, is not to celebrate the newfound (apparent) prudence of technology executives, it is to recognize what their comments reveal. When even fierce rivals begin to argue for mutual scrutiny, they are admitting that competition alone cannot govern the frontier. That admission should be treated not as reassurance but as evidence that the risk has become collective.

The policy task now is to build institutions that fit that reality. Governments should push for mandatory reporting, independent evaluation and legal backstops. But they should also encourage enforceable forms of peer oversight among the handful of firms whose systems may shape the trajectory of the technology. Frontier AI is becoming an industry in which the leading actors are hostages of one another. The nuclear age showed that such conditions can produce serious governance. The hope is that AI firms learn that lesson before they learn the cost of ignoring it at the peril of the public at large.

articles.title: Arizona's Otherworldly 'Wonderland of Rocks' Is Now America's Newest National Park

paras.en: America’s newest national park protects thousands of years of human history, nearly 200 species of birds and towering stone spires formed by an ancient volcanic eruption.

Chiricahua National Monument in southeastern Arizona is now Chiricahua National Park, bringing the total number of national parks in the United States to 64. Nicknamed the “Wonderland of Rocks,” the site has been a national monument since 1924 but was officially redesignated as a national park this week.
Chiricahua—pronounced “cheery-cow-uh”—is the country’s first new national park in six years, following the establishment of West Virginia’s New River Gorge National Park and Preserve in 2020.

The 12,000-acre park protects part of the Chiricahua Mountains, one of several “sky islands,” or isolated mountain ranges that rise up from the surrounding deserts of southeastern Arizona and northern Mexico. Located about 120 miles from Tucson, it sits at the intersection of four major ecosystems: the Rocky Mountains, Sierra Madre, Sonoran Desert and Chihuahuan Desert.

In 2025, Chiricahua National Monument welcomed 70,406 visitors, ranking 254th out of 399 National Park Service sites. Business owners, outdoor groups, politicians and others hope that number will increase following its national park designation, Henry Brean reports for the Arizona Daily Star.

Chiricahua’s unique geology is a big part of the appeal for visitors. About 27 million years ago, a massive volcanic eruption blanketed the region in ash and debris. Over time, that material hardened into a rock layer called rhyolitic tuff. Millions of years of wind, rain, freezing temperatures and other natural forces gradually wore it away, carving the landscape into a maze of towering stone spires, balanced boulders and narrow passageways.

“It has spectacular vistas,” Emily Burns, program director for the Sky Island Alliance, a regional conservation nonprofit, tells USA Today’s Ignacio Calderón and Janet Loehrke. “It has a beautiful canyon and then these rock formations that are a little mind-boggling to understand how they formed over geologic history.”

Visitors can explore the otherworldly landscape via the park’s 17 miles of hiking trails. As Sylvia Dekker writes for Outside magazine, trekking through the national park feels like “being dwarfed by a sea of massive navigation cairns and those knobby towers of dribbled sand children make at the beach.”

Scenic drives, stargazing, horseback riding and camping are also popular ways to experience the park. Surrounded by the 1.78-million-acre Coronado National Forest, it’s also a haven for wildlife, giving animal lovers the chance to spot everything from Coues deer and javelina to black bears, mountain lions, coatimundi, skunks and 16 species of bats.

Birdwatchers also flock here to see the migratory species that pass through on their way to and from Mexico and Central and South America, as well as the many resident species that live in the area year-round. Around 200 bird species have been documented in the park.

Human history in the Chiricahua region stretches back at least 12,000 years, when paleoindians hunted big game in the area. Later, hunter-gatherers took advantage of its diverse plants and wildlife before some communities turned to agriculture.

The Chiricahua Apache lived across a vast territory spanning present-day southeastern Arizona, southwestern New Mexico and northern Mexico. Conflict with the U.S. government eventually culminated in the Apache’s forced removal in the late 19th century. The area was also home to Buffalo Soldiers, homesteaders, immigrants and Civilian Conservation Corps laborers.

Today, the park offers visitors a chance to experience this landscape much as generations before them have. One of the biggest perks of visiting Chiricahua is the ability to “immerse yourself in a place that seems relatively unchanged over the millennia,” Matthew Nelson, executive director of the nonprofit Arizona Trail Association, tells USA Today.

“[It’s] just such a break from modern day technology and the pace of our lives,” Nelson adds. “Being in the rocks in Chiricahua encourages people to just slow down and to listen to the wind and to study the rock features and to be reminded of the beauty that exists in nature.”

articles.title: More Than 1,000 Birds Were Killed or Injured in Window Collisions Around Chicago Over the Weekend

paras.en: Wildlife advocates are sounding the alarm after more than 1,000 birds were killed or injured in window collisions in the Chicago area last weekend, reports Fox 32 Chicago’s Nic Flosi.

Volunteers with the nonprofit Chicago Bird Collision Monitors spent October 17 and 18 rescuing wounded birds and collecting the bodies of dead ones in downtown Chicago and the northern suburb of Evanston.

“We’d pick up a bird at a building, go around that building, and immediately find another,” Annette Prince, director of Chicago Bird Collision Monitors, tells the Chicago Sun-Times’ Kaitlin Washburn. “We had birds hitting the glass windows over our heads.”

Prince says the more than 1,000 birds collected by volunteers likely represent only a fraction of those injured or killed during this year’s fall migration—or even over the weekend. They searched a small area, and they can “only find what’s on the ground,” Prince tells WTTW’s Patty Wetli. Many more birds probably go undiscovered, she says.
“We don’t even know the full extent, and that’s very sobering,” she adds. “What’s heartbreaking to us is this happens year after year.”

More than five million birds flew through Cook County, which includes Chicago, on the evening of October 16, according to the Cornell Lab of Ornithology’s BirdCast, which uses weather radar to detect and predict migratory activity. That huge number of birds coincided with a cold front, which brought favorable northerly tailwinds that can help push birds south. Across the country, more than one billion migratory birds were estimated to have taken flight that night.

Chicago is located along the Mississippi Flyway, a major migratory corridor for millions of birds traveling between North, Central and South America every spring and fall. But the city’s abundance of windows and artificial lights can make it a hazardous place for birds to navigate.

Birds often don’t see transparent glass, or they mistake its reflections of the surrounding scenery for a clear path forward. As a result, they can end up crashing into windows while traveling at speeds of up to 30 miles per hour, which can cause death, internal bleeding, concussions or other injuries. Artificial lights can also attract and disorient birds, increasing the risk of collisions, particularly at night, when many species migrate.

The birds that make it to Chicago every spring and fall, Prince tells WTTW, are “fit and strong.” But the city’s lights and windows are “taking out the best members,” she says. “They were doing everything right.”

Wildlife advocates say these deaths are largely preventable, an especially urgent concern at a time when bird populations face mounting threats. North America has lost around three billion birds since 1970, a figure that represents about 29 percent of the continent’s population, or more than one in four birds. In many places, the rate of decline is accelerating, likely due to warming temperatures and intensive agriculture, research suggests.

Chicago has seen high numbers of deadly bird collisions before. In October 2023, nearly 1,000 birds died in a single night after crashing into McCormick Place Lakeside Center, an event venue with a primarily glass facade.

Ahead of the 2024 fall migration, the building’s managers spent $1.2 million installing a special, polka-dot-covered film designed to help birds better differentiate between windows and open air. The center also vowed to implement other bird-safe measures, such as switching off non-essential exterior lights and closing drapes and blinds at night. Those efforts led to a more than 90 percent reduction in bird collision deaths during the following autumn season.

Wildlife advocates would like Chicago’s leaders to mandate such bird safety design measures for all new and renovated buildings. They’re pushing city councilors to adopt a bird-friendly building ordinance that’s currently undergoing language revisions in the city’s zoning committee, per the Chicago Tribune’s Adriana Pérez. Similar laws have been passed in other major cities, including New York City and Washington, D.C.

Birds “have a right to migrate and live and fly through our city without unnecessary harm,” Jennifer Bell, a Chicago Bird Collision Monitors volunteer who estimates she has collected more than 350 birds since September on her own, tells Block Club Chicago’s Janelle Mella. “We are causing unnecessary harm by continuing to build all of these glass buildings.”

articles.title: Researchers Claimed a Blurry Object on Apple Maps Was 'Very Likely' Amelia Earhart's Missing Plane. It Turned Out to Be a 'Collection of Large Trees'

paras.en: The expedition began with a blurry satellite image on Apple Maps. Just off Nikumaroro, a remote atoll in the South Pacific, a mysterious object lurked below the surface. Didn’t it look suspiciously like the wing of an airplane?

The atoll in question is located near the region where aviator Amelia Earhart and her navigator, Fred Noonan, disappeared in 1937. The location of their Lockheed Electra has been a longstanding mystery, but that hasn’t stopped new generations of sleuths from trying to solve it. The strange shape near Nikumaroro sparked the latest attempt to crack the case.

Earlier this month, a team of 17 traveled to the South Pacific to investigate the so-called Taraia Object, named for the atoll’s Taraia Peninsula. They surveyed the site with a magnetometer (to detect ferrous metals) and side-scan sonar (to identify objects buried in the sediment). As they worked, onlookers eagerly anticipated success, with some headlines claiming that the 89-year-old mystery “could be solved in days.”

On October 18, the researchers announced the results: They had found “no conclusive evidence” of Earhart’s plane on Nikumaroro. That tantalizing shape in the satellite imagery had likely been “a collection of large trees.” Many of the trees and other debris had already washed away by the time the team arrived at the site.

“The name ‘Taraia’ itself in the Gilbertese language, the Kiribati language, can mean ‘see if you can find it,’” Steve Schultz, Purdue University’s general counsel and a member of the expedition, says in a video. “We came to see what we could find here, to see if it could add a final concluding chapter to the mystery of Amelia Earhart and Fred Noonan’s disappearance. And unfortunately, we weren’t able to find that smoking gun.”

When her plane disappeared, Earhart was trying to become the first woman in history to fly around the world. She’d already broken a number of other records, becoming the first woman (and second person) to fly solo and nonstop across the Atlantic in 1932 and the first person to fly solo and nonstop from Hawaii to the United States mainland in 1935. Two years later, she plotted out a round-the-world journey divided into 34 legs. She selected a route near the equator to avoid harsh northern weather. In exchange, however, she would need to navigate long stretches of open water in the South Pacific.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Earhart and Noonan took off from Lae, New Guinea, on July 2, 1937. Their plan was to land on Howland Island, an isolated speck of earth thousands of miles from the mainland, where a Coast Guard cutter waited with fuel. “We must be on you, but we cannot see you,” the aviator radioed as she approached her destination. “Fuel is running low. Been unable to reach you by radio. We are flying at 1,000 feet.” About an hour later, she made her final transmission to the vessel: “We are running north and south.” Earhart and Noonan disappeared after completing nearly 31 of their 34 legs. They had flown 22,000 of their planned 29,000 miles.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - After the Electra disappeared, rescuers conducted a large-scale search covering 250,000 square miles of ocean. The Navy ultimately concluded that the plane had likely crashed in the Pacific.

- “Although unfortunately the fate of the missing flyers remains a mystery, it is considered that the search made was efficient and that the areas covered were the most probable ones, based on the facts and information available,” the Navy wrote in a report later that month.

Numerous far-fetched theories have attempted to explain the pair’s disappearance. Some conspiracy theorists believe that Earhart landed in the Marshall Islands, where she was captured by the Japanese. One of them published a 2016 book claiming that President Franklin D. Roosevelt had sent the aviator on a secret spy mission, with Earhart later returning to America under a new identity.

Most experts think that the plane went down in the ocean near Howland Island. But some argue that Earhart and Noonan landed on Nikumaroro, some 400 miles away, and died there as castaways. Researchers with the International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery (TIGHAR) have made numerous trips to the island, where they identified several 1930s-era cosmetic items and fragments of a shoe. These discoveries are titillating, but none of them are definitively linked to the Electra. The shoe, for example, likely wasn’t Earhart’s size.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The castaway theory “doesn’t follow the facts,” Dorothy Cochrane, then a curator at the Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum, told Smithsonian magazine’s Brigit Katz in 2019. The Coast Guard cutter waiting near Howland Island reported that her radio transmissions had gotten progressively louder, suggesting that she was getting closer. Rescuers flew over Nikumaroro within a week of the disappearance; if she were there, “it’s just inconceivable that they would not have seen her,” said Cochrane, who retired last year.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Several other big-budget expeditions have come up empty in recent years. In 2019, Robert Ballard, the oceanographer who discovered the wreck of the Titanic, conducted an unsuccessful search. In 2024, the exploration company Deep Sea Vision identified an intriguing shape on a sonar image some 100 miles from Howland Island; it later found that this shape was a natural rock formation.

The recent investigation began with Michael Ashmore, the amateur researcher who found the blurry Apple Maps image in 2020. He contacted Richard Gillespie, TIGHAR’s executive director, who wasn’t convinced. After all, TIGHAR’s researchers had previously investigated that section of the island.

But the satellite image intrigued Richard Pettigrew, executive director of the Archaeological Legacy Institute, who asked Ashmore to present his discovery at a conference. “I was sufficiently impressed,” Pettigrew told National Geographic’s Rachel Hartigan earlier this month. “Within a few days after that, I was already looking for ways to get back to Nikumaroro.”

Pettigrew created a video about the theory, which caught the attention of Schultz at Purdue. As it happens, Earhart had worked as a consultant and career counselor at the university. She even purchased the Electra with money from the Purdue Research Foundation—and, according to the university’s announcement, she had planned to return the plane to Purdue after her record-breaking flight.

Purdue University and the Purdue Research Foundation partnered with the Archaeological Legacy Institute to plan the Taraia Object expedition. Ahead of the trip, the researchers were bullish. “We believe it is very likely that the Taraia Object in Nikumaroro Lagoon is actually the remains of the Lockheed Model 10-E Electra flown to the island by Amelia Earhart and Fred Noonan,” they wrote. They described the expedition as “Phase 1 of a potential three-phase project,” which could eventually include “full-scale archaeological excavation (Phase 2) and recovery (Phase 3) of the aircraft remains.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Despite the disappointing results, the researchers are eager to continue the search. They say their confidence in the castaway theory hasn’t faltered. “There’s a long list of evidence that supports that conclusion,” Pettigrew says in the video. “I think eventually someone will find conclusive evidence here to finally put a cap on the mystery.”

Other experts, however, doubt that any evidence will surface on Nikumaroro. Nauticos, the deep-sea exploration company, is raising money for its fourth attempt to locate Earhart’s plane, which will investigate an area near Howland Island. “I’m very excited about their work,” Cochrane tells CTV’s Anne-Marie Mediwake. “They’re following the facts of the flight.”

articles.title: Best Pet Camera of 2026: Furbo, Petcube, and Enabot
articles.author: Molly Higgins

paras.en: The best pet camera for you depends on what you value for your pet. Personally, I never knew I needed a pet camera, but after trying several models, I don’t think I can go into the office or on vacation without one set up at home. A home security camera can give you extra peace of mind when you’re out, and pet cameras specifically designed for our furry friends add helpful features, like the ability to follow your pet around, engage in play, and dispense kibble. Connected to an app on your phone and with cloud storage options, these pet cameras—including our top pick for most people (and pets!), the Furbo Mini 360° ($49), and our compact 360 rotating budget pick, Petcube Cam 360 ($47)—ensure you’ll never miss a moment in your pet’s life when you’re away (or at home).

It also has the expected pet camera-on-wheels features, like two-way audio and video, night vision, and 4K imaging. During initial testing, the camera didn't charge properly on the dock and often froze or stopped charging. I got a second model to test, and it worked better—it handled tasks on command, returned to the charging station, and recognized my cats. However, I still don't think its AI-powered companion features are cool enough to justify that price tag. If price is no issue for you and you want a moving camera on wheels, it's worth checking out.

paras.en: Security cameras let you keep an eye on your house (and pet) while you’re away, but pet cameras often include additional pet-specific features, such as the ability to dispense treats and interact with your furry friend via a two-way speaker. These cameras with special features can help ease common pet issues like separation anxiety or boredom. The Enabot Rola PetPal Robot Pet Companion, for example, has attachments that let you remotely give your pet a treat or engage in “playtime.”

That's not to say you can’t use a security camera as a pet cam, but like any other smart home device that connects to Wi-Fi, it could be hacked and compromise your privacy. Make sure your Wi-Fi password is strong, and set up two-factor authentication in your camera’s app. It’s also a good idea to keep it turned off when you’re home, as an extra precaution.

articles.title: New mRNA Vaccine Reduces Risk of Melanoma Recurrence by Over 40 Percent
articles.author: Fernanda González

paras.en: An experimental vaccine offers new hope to patients with melanoma, one of the most aggressive forms of skin cancer. The pharmaceutical companies Merck and Moderna released the results of a Phase 3 clinical trial that evaluated the efficacy of a personalized mRNA-based vaccine that, when combined with immunotherapy, reduced the risk of disease recurrence or death by 42 percent compared to treatment with the immunotherapy drug alone.

Georgina Long, medical director of the Australian Melanoma Institute and the study’s principal investigator, said in a statement that these results are “transformative” and “have the potential to make a foundational shift in how we treat patients with earlier-stage melanoma.”

The trial, known as INTerpath-001, included 1,137 people with high-risk melanoma who had undergone surgery to completely remove their tumors. The participants were divided into two groups. Those in the first group received only Pembrolizumab, a drug that helps the immune system detect and fight cancer cells, while those in the second group were treated with the same drug in combination with the mRNA vaccine, called Intismeran Autogene.

After monitoring the participants for an average of 24.6 months, the researchers determined that addition of the vaccine reduced the risk of cancer recurrence or death by 42 percent compared to Pembrolizumab alone.

The results also showed that the experimental treatment reduced the risk of the disease spreading to other parts of the body by 38 percent. At the end of the follow-up period, 82.2 percent of patients who received both treatments remained recurrence-free, compared with 70 percent of those who received Pembrolizumab alone.

“The results of the INTerpath-001 study represent a major breakthrough in the treatment of melanoma and, in particular, in the development of personalized medicine,” Eva Muñoz Couselo—who leads a melanoma research group at the Vall d’Hebron Institute of Oncology, in Barcelona and who was not involved in the study—told SMC Spain. “For the first time, a Phase III trial has demonstrated that an individualized therapeutic vaccine, designed on the basis of the molecular characteristics of each patient’s tumor, can significantly improve the outcomes of conventional immunotherapy.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The laboratories explained that the vaccine was developed from a tumor sample taken from each patient, which was used to identify specific mutations that would create distinct proteins the immune system could learn to recognize in order to attack cancer cells. The scientists selected up to three of these molecular signatures per patient.

During the trial, some participants experienced mild side effects such as fever, fatigue, and pain at the injection site. These side effects were seen in earlier trials as well, and the Phase 3 findings demonstrate similar safety when the vaccine is used in the combination with Pembrolizumab.
“These results reinforce our conviction that mRNA has the potential to fundamentally change how we treat cancer,” Stéphane Bancel, CEO of Moderna, said in a statement.

The pharmaceutical companies emphasized that the vaccine is not designed to prevent melanoma but rather to reduce the risk of recurrence and death following prior medical treatment. They also noted that the therapy remains under investigation to validate its efficacy and obtain approval from health authorities before widespread use.

Most people diagnosed with melanoma have a high chance of survival, especially if detected early, but as one of the most common cancers, melanoma kills over 50,000 people globally each year. In theory, similar vaccines could be developed for other kinds of tumors in the future. Earlier this year, another trial demonstrated that personalized mRNA vaccines can greatly improve survival among patients with pancreatic cancer, one of the deadliest kinds of tumor.

“This is the major breakthrough, because conceptually it would make it possible to treat not only melanoma but also other tumors in which the immune system can be reactivated,” Marisol Soengas—a leading melanoma researcher at Spain’s National Cancer Research Center also not involved in the trial—told SMC Spain.

That doesn’t mean a cure for cancer is right around the corner. “The challenge is to ensure that this personalization can be scaled up to a large number of patients and that the cost is affordable for health care systems,” Soengas said. “It is logistically complex. It is literally a bespoke vaccine.”
This story originally appeared on WIRED en Español and has been translated from Spanish.

articles.title: The PHP Meltdown Shows How AI Makes Bugs More Exploitable
articles.author: Lily Hay Newman, Matt Burgess

paras.en: As security teams and web admins scrambled this week to patch newly public PHP bugs, criminal hackers quickly attempted to exploit the flaws in the wild. Millions of exploitation attempts hit within hours of the vulnerabilities being published, according to analysis from Cloudflare—unsurprising given broad access to AI tools that can make it easier for attackers to quickly exploit flaws.

So far, the nightmare scenario of mass victim takeovers and breaches hasn’t come to pass. The PHP Foundation says it hasn’t seen any successful exploitation of the bugs, collectively dubbed PHP2Shell, and many publicly circulating potential exploits appear to be ineffective. However, perhaps the most interesting role of AI amid the chaos this week is how advanced models helped researchers uncover practical exploitations for the vulnerabilities, which were known about, at least in part, for years. In other words, AI helped turn historic vulnerability into a current crisis.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: So are we all about to be walloped by a wave of critical vulnerabilities that have been kicking around for decades?

Researchers at security company Calif were the first to identify the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities and create exploits in early August—partially using frontier AI tools as part of OpenAI’s Patch the Planet program, but also using expert human knowledge of PHP, its dynamics, and its weaknesses. Some of the underlying issues were identified in 2024 but were deemed too complex to exploit at the time. Following Calif’s discovery, researchers at OpenAI and the Google-owned security firm Wiz independently discovered PHP2Shell flaws using AI tools.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “The vulnerability had been known to the PHP team for years, but because it could not be leveraged by an attacker—at least, not a human one—it was not addressed,” says Sagi Tzadik, a security researcher at Wiz.

No software is perfect. There are inevitably flaws in even the most critical, foundational digital tools, but the expanding capabilities of AI models have made it faster to analyze and potentially exploit vulnerabilities. This puts even more pressure on under-resourced IT teams, developers, and admins to keep up. Microsoft’s security updates included a record 1,453 security vulnerabilities this month alone. Meanwhile, Bank of America recently hired 1,000 consultants to fix flaws discovered by Anthropic’s Mythos. Security researchers emphasize, though, that AI is ultimately not doing anything new, but rather magnifying existing dynamics of vulnerability discovery and coordinated disclosure.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “We'll definitely see more of these long-life bugs that are in every version of the software for the last decade or whatever,” says Jake Williams, vice president of research and development at Hunter Strategy and a former NSA hacker. “But I think there’s only so much of this low-hanging fruit. There isn’t much else that has the specific reach of PHP. It’s a pretty wild attack surface—most other tools aren’t exposed to the internet by design.”

Researchers note, too, that even with frontier models, most examples of sophisticated AI-aided hacking also involve human expertise. As Ryan Austin, the Calif researcher who first discovered the PHP flaws, wrote this week, “No model is simply capable of unearthing ‘all bugs’ with simple prompts. At least for now.”

In short, security engineer and researcher Niels Provos says, everyone can dial back their freak-outs, at least a bit. “To be honest, I am not really worried,” he says, about AI finding an overwhelming number of historic bugs that are newly exploitable—or new vulnerabilities that couldn’t have been practically exploited without AI. “People have now been looking with AI for over a year, and it required a highly skilled team to find this one. I guess we will see whether I am completely wrong, but I doubt it.”

articles.title: On This Day, Oct. 24: Annie Edson Taylor is first person to go over Niagara Falls in barrel

paras.en: Oct. 24 (UPI) -- On this date in history:
In 1901, daredevil Annie Edson Taylor became the first person to go over Niagara Falls in a barrel.

In 1929, $5 billion in market values were swept away in the greatest selling wave in the history of the New York Stock Exchange. The Wall Street Crash of 1929 would mark the beginning of a 10-year Depression which would affect the entire Western world.
In 1931, New York City's George Washington Bridge opened to public traffic.
In 1962, the blockade of Cuba was in effect, with a ring of U.S. warships and planes under orders to block by whatever means, further aggressive arm deliveries to Fidel Castro.
In 1992, the Toronto Blue Jays become the first Major League Baseball team based outside the United States to win the World Series.

In 2002, police arrested two suspects in a three-week series of Washington-area sniper attacks that killed 10 people and wounded three others. John Allen Muhammad, 41, and John Lee Malvo, 17, were found sleeping in a car at a rest stop near Frederick, Md. Both were convicted. Muhammad was executed and Malvo sentenced to life in prison.
In 2003, an era in aviation history ended when the supersonic Concorde took off from New York to London on its final flight.

In 2009, U.S. President Barack Obama declared a national emergency related to the outbreak of the H1N1 flu virus, also known as swine flu, to aid local authorities in dealing with the pandemic. Medical officials put the American death toll at 530 with thousands hospitalized.
In 2012, a 41-mile final stretch of Texas Highway 130, a toll road from Mustang Ridge, south of Austin, to Seguin, opened with the highest speed limit in the United States -- 85 mph.

In 2012, Hurricane Sandy made landfall for the first time, in Jamaica, killing two people there. The storm would go on to cause tens of billions of dollars in the northeast United States and kill more than 200 people along its path.

In 2021, Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Tom Brady made his record 600th touchdown pass during a game against the Chicago Bears. During the game, the ball was given to a fan, who returned it to the team in exchange for a replacement game ball and a $1,000 gift certificate to the team store. Experts told UPI the original ball was likely worth $500,000 to $1 million. Brady retired in 2022 with 649 touchdown passes.
In 2022, silent movie actor Anna May Wong became the first Asian American to be featured on U.S. currency as part of the U.S. mint's American Women Quarters Program.

In 2024, Grammy award-winning rapper Lil Durk, recognized as the creative leader of Chicago's "drill" hip-hop scene, was arrested and held without bond in Florida on a charge of murder for hire. He pleaded not guilty to the charge.

articles.title: Hitler's Eagle's Nest destroyed by fire; 1 man arrested

paras.en: Oct. 24 (UPI) -- Adolf Hitler's mountain retreat in the Bavarian Alps was gutted by fire, and one man has been arrested.

The Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle's Nest, caught fire Friday night, setting off alarms at 9:25 p.m. local time in nearby Traunstein. Firefighters arrived to find the building engulfed in flames.

Fire trucks had some difficulty getting access to the site "due to the local conditions," authorities said. The building is about 6,000 feet up in the Kehlstein mountain, and visitors had to access it via a long tunnel leading to an elevator that travels up about 40 stories. Only specially designed buses have regular access to the road to the tunnel.
The fire was still burning early Saturday, police said, with about 200 emergency personnel on the scene. No injuries were reported.
Police said Saturday that the building wasn't likely salvageable. They also offered no details about the person arrested, saying the investigation was ongoing.

The building was completed in 1938 and was a guesthouse for Nazi officials and their visitors. Hitler also used the area as a backdrop for propaganda films showing him as a lover of animals and nature.
It became a tourist attraction in the 1950s, and until Friday offered Alpine views and a restaurant. The Kehlstein mountain is a subpeak of the Hoher Gӧll, which overlooks the town of Berchtesgaten.

Farther down the mountain is the Obersalzburg Documentation Center, which tells the story of the building and Nazi use of the site and offers entrance to some of the mountain tunnels where Nazis hid during the war.
The Kehlsteinhaus and the mountain tunnels and bunkers were graffitied by Allied soldiers who liberated the area.

articles.title: Maluma Opens Up About Therapy and Finding Balance at Billboard Latin Music Week & More Uplifting Moments
articles.author: Isabela Raygoza

paras.en: From career milestones to new music releases to major announcements and those little important moments, Billboard editors highlight uplifting moments in Latin music. Here’s what happened in the Latin music world this week.
Maluma on Mental Health, Fatherhood and Learning to “Love Discomfort”

Maluma spoke candidly about therapy, anxiety, fatherhood and the challenge of balancing family life with a demanding career during the “Like Minded” conversation at Billboard Latin Music Week on Wednesday (Oct. 21). Moderated by Billboard’s co-chief content officer Leila Cobo, the BetterHelp-presented session also featured bilingual therapist Patricia Arrieta.

The conversation came shortly after the birth of Maluma’s second child, Orion, whom he said has brought him a new sense of calm and clarity. “I’ve finally been able to find that balance between my personal life and my artistic career,” he said. The Colombian star described therapy as an ongoing practice rather than a quick fix. “For me, therapy is being quiet, it is meditation, it’s constantly feeling uncomfortable and learning to love that discomfort,” he said.

Maluma acknowledged that he still experiences anxiety while managing his responsibilities as a father, artist, entrepreneur and leader of a large team. After undergoing a tension headache during an especially demanding week, he used ChatGPT to help organize his schedule and prioritize his well-being. “I started prioritizing my peace, lowering my burdens and stress,” he said. “I need at least four hours in the afternoon to spend with my family.”

He also spoke about moving away from extreme approaches to fitness and developing a healthier relationship with food and his body. “If you love yourself, you make good decisions,” he said. “My health is not negotiable.”

Reflecting on his latest album, Loco por Volver, Maluma said the project became part of his personal transformation. “It was the album that gave me back so many things I had lost,” he said. “The music transformed me.”
“Help is closer than we think,” he added.
Pablo Alborán & RIZA Turn a Latin Music Week Collab Into a Finished Song at Billboard Latin Music Awards

What began as a live songwriting experiment at last year’s Billboard Latin Music Week became a finished release — and then a Billboard Latin Music Awards performance on Thursday (Oct. 22). Pablo Alborán and RIZA delivered “Deditos Cruzados,” the dreamy collaboration they created during last year’s “Making the Hit, Live!” panel with producer Julio Reyes Copello and engineer Natalia Schlesinger.

Released Oct. 1, the song blends soulful vocals, Middle Eastern-tinged rhythms and lyrics about longing. Onstage, the pair performed from a warm, living room-inspired set, turning a creative experiment born in front of an audience into a full-circle musical moment. Check out “Deditos Cruzados” live below.
Nanpa Básico and Nella Bring Hope During Billboard Latin Music Awards After Colombia and Venezuela Earthquakes

Colombian artist Nanpa Básico and Venezuelan singer Nella delivered a moving rendition of “Todo Cambia,” the classic written by Julio Numhauser and famously popularized by Mercedes Sosa. Their Billboard Latin Music Awards performance on Thursday (Oct. 22) acknowledged the devastation caused by earthquakes that hit their home countries. Images of shattered buildings and concrete paved way to green plants emerging from the rubble. Nella sang beside the wreckage in a flowing brown gown, while Nanpa brought a cowboy-inspired touch to the bittersweet duet. By the end, the stage had transformed into a portrait of renewal — a reminder that, even after tragedy, something hopeful can grow. See their performance below.
